papers.abstract_en: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

papers.abstract_en: D2C7-ATC is a recombinant antibody-toxin conjugate (ATC) targeting wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutant EGFR variant III (EGFRvIII). We conducted a single-arm, single-site, open-label phase 1 trial evaluating a single infusion of D2C7-ATC via convection-enhanced delivery in the enhancing disease of 81 patients with biopsy-confirmed recurrent malignant glioma. The primary objective was to determine toxicity and the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of D2C7-ATC. Secondary objectives included describing overall survival (OS) and assessing the association between EGFR expression and OS. The median overall survival (mOS) was 7.9 months among 72 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type recurrent glioblastoma (IDHwt rGBM), including 35 patients in the dose-escalation stage (40 to 35,032 ng ml-1) and 37 patients in the dose-expansion stage (RP2D of 6,920 ng ml-1). D2C7-ATC was generally well tolerated, with mainly grade 1-2 treatment-related adverse events (67%). The maximum tolerated dose was exceeded at 35,032 ng ml-1, where four patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities, including grade 4 (N = 2) and grade 3 (N = 2) events. Eight patients died on trial; all deaths were unrelated to D2C7-ATC. Univariate analyses identified survival-associated biomarkers, including tumor D2C7 antibody reactivity, circulating cytokines, a tumor inflammatory gene signature and neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes in blood. Notably, patients with IDHwt rGBM with a D2C7 antibody reactivity score of <1.5+ in pre-treatment tumor had an mOS of 17.38 months, whereas those with low IL-8 in post-treatment plasma had an mOS of 16.6 months. These findings indicate that EGFR-targeted D2C7-ATC therapy prolongs survival in a subset of patients with IDHwt rGBM via intratumoral and systemic immune activation. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02303678 .

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. papers.abstract_en: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane-localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Phospholipid metabolism (PLM) has been implicated in macrophage polarization and tumor progression in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Metabolic intermediates such as lysophosphatidylcholine modulate macrophage surface receptor signaling, while inhibition of phospholipid synthesis may attenuate tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) infiltration and suppress LUAD progression. However, macrophage-centered PLM-related prognostic signatures in LUAD remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We performed an integrative multi-omics analysis combining single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk transcriptomic profiling, and clinical data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. Macrophage-related genes (MacRGs) were identified using single-cell analysis and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA). Phospholipid metabolism-related module genes were determined through differential expression analysis and WGCNA. Candidate genes were prioritized using machine learning and Cox regression analyses, followed by construction and external validation of a multigene risk model. Functional enrichment, immune microenvironment profiling, mutation landscape analysis, estimated drug sensitivity, and pseudotime trajectory analyses were performed to explore the biological relevance of the signature. Experimental validation was conducted using LUAD tissues and cell models. RESULTS: A four-gene macrophage-PLM-related signature was constructed to calculate a risk score that stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different overall survival. The risk score and T stage were independent prognostic factors, and an integrated nomogram showed acceptable prognostic performance. Functional analyses revealed distinct metabolic and signaling pathway enrichment patterns between risk groups, with 40 shared pathways across the four hub genes. The high-risk group exhibited an altered immune microenvironment characterized by differential infiltration of 20 immune cell subsets, immune checkpoint expression changes, lower ESTIMATE scores, and distinct TIDE profiles. Somatic mutation patterns and tumor mutational burden differed between groups. Drug-sensitivity estimation identified 105 compounds with differential estimated IC50 values between risk groups. DPYSL2 expression was associated with macrophage polarization dynamics, and DPYSL2 overexpression suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and clonogenicity in vitro. CONCLUSION: We identified a macrophage-phospholipid metabolism-associated four-gene prognostic signature that provides prognostic information and reflects immune-metabolic remodeling in LUAD. These findings support further investigation of macrophage-phospholipid metabolism-related genes as candidate biomarkers and may inform future therapeutic stratification studies in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in lung cancer may be coded as immune, marrow suppression, coagulation, or non-specific. We tested whether coding-defined report phenotypes differed across co-reported treatment contexts. METHODS: We analyzed FAERS (2015Q1-2026Q2) and JADER through Japanese fiscal 2025Q4 (31 March 2026). Strict primary lung cancer reports were grouped as ICI without chemotherapy (C1), ICI plus chemotherapy (C2), or chemotherapy without ICI (C3). Firth models compared mutually exclusive immune-like and marrow-like anchors. Complementary analyses evaluated the broad cohort, treatment date compatibility, C3 small-cell influence, phenotype variants, onset windows, treatment-variable ablation in elastic-net report phenotype models, and a 120-report random stratified blinded review with independent ratings, third-person adjudication, inverse-selection weighting, and bootstrap uncertainty. RESULTS: FAERS included 1,362 immune-like or marrow-like anchors. Relative to C1, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for immune-like versus marrow-like phenotype were 0.111 (95% CI, 0.069-0.173) in C2 and 0.014 (0.006-0.029) in C3; C3 was exploratory because only eight reports were immune-like. In 2,835 broad cohort reports, adjusted immune-like composition was 13.0% (95% bootstrap interval, 11.0%-15.1%) in C1 and 4.7% (3.4%-6.2%) in C2. Treatment date and stricter phenotype analyses were directionally consistent. JADER reproduced the C2 versus C1 direction but showed calibration shift; treatment-variable ablation reduced cross-database discrimination. Reviewers agreed on 111/120 reports (92.5%; 95% CI, 87.5%-96.7%; Cohen's κ, 0.897; Gwet's AC1, 0.901). In the locked 927-report frame, design-weighted final categories were 23.4% immune probable, 37.3% immune possible, 13.6% indeterminate, and 25.8% non-immune probable. Among 100 determinate reports, weighted AUROC was 0.892 (0.827-0.948), PR-AUC 0.956 (0.922-0.982), and calibration-in-the-large intercept 2.054 (1.707-2.432), indicating underprediction. CONCLUSION: Coding-defined thrombocytopenia report composition differed across treatment contexts. Blinded review supported reproducible structured category assignment and score-based report ordering, while calibration shift and treatment-variable ablation defined important limits. Findings support pharmacovigilance case prioritization and hypothesis generation, not clinical diagnosis, incidence estimation, patient-level etiologic attribution, or causal inference.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation (AE) is the most lethal event of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD). This exploratory study compared clinical, radiomics, and combined predictor strategies across five survival-learning algorithms for survival risk stratification. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 78 patients with AE-IIM-ILD and divided them into a training cohort (n = 54; 20 deaths) and a held-out internal testing cohort (n = 24; 9 deaths), stratified by observed mortality event status. Three predictor strategies were evaluated: a clinical strategy comprising PaO2/FiO2 ratio, neutrophil percentage (NEU%), and arthritis-related symptoms; a radiomics strategy comprising two selected radiomics features; and a combined strategy comprising PaO2/FiO2 ratio, arthritis-related symptoms, and a composite radiomics score (Rad-score). Each strategy was evaluated using five survival-learning algorithms. Harrell's concordance index (C-index) was the primary discrimination metric, with mean time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) used as a secondary measure. RESULTS: During the 1-year follow-up, 29 deaths were observed. Performance rankings varied across predictor strategies, algorithms, and evaluation metrics. The combined-Random Survival Forest configuration demonstrated the highest training-cohort C-index among the 15 configurations. Its mean time-dependent AUC was 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.970) in the training cohort and 0.915 (95% CI: 0.736-0.986) in the testing cohort, with corresponding C-indices of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.803-0.940) and 0.842 (95% CI: 0.673-0.971), respectively. The model stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct observed survival trajectories. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory cohort, integrating selected clinical variables with a quantitative CT Rad-score using RSF showed promising numerical discrimination and risk-stratification performance. These findings suggest that clinical and quantitative imaging information may provide complementary prognostic information after AE-IIM-ILD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are biologically distinct yet interconnected components of antitumor immunity. ICD promotes danger-associated immune activation, whereas TLSs organize local adaptive immune responses. However, how these processes jointly affect immune heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic responsiveness in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. METHODS: To define the coordinated roles of TLS- and ICD-related programs in LUAD, we used a multi-cohort and multi-layer analytical framework. This framework included transcriptomic analysis, Mendelian randomization, consensus machine-learning prognostic modeling, immune landscape characterization, single-cell RNA sequencing, multiplex immunohistochemistry, immunotherapy response assessment, exploratory drug screening, structural analyses, and multilayer network topology analysis. RESULTS: TLS- and ICD-associated genes were transcriptionally dysregulated in LUAD. By integrating 13 machine-learning algorithms, we developed 801 candidate prognostic models and identified optimal TLS- and ICD-related models that stratified patients effectively into high- and low-risk groups. These models showed strong performance in TCGA and remained robust across six external cohorts. Low-risk tumors had higher TLS+ICD scores than high-risk tumors. Immune landscape analysis indicated that low-risk tumors had elevated immune scores, enhanced antigen presentation, cytotoxic T/NK-cell signatures, checkpoint activation, and lower Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) scores, suggesting a more immunotherapy-responsive microenvironment. Consistently, higher TLS+ICD scores correlated with improved survival and greater immunotherapy responsiveness in independent cohorts. Mendelian randomization and survival analyses prioritized CD40, CD5, and GFI1 as candidate TLS-ICD immune-regulatory genes, with single-cell and mIHC analyses defining their major cellular origins, spatial protein phenotypes, and prognostic relevance. Drug prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations identified CAY10576, SCH772984, and SZ4TA2 as potential therapeutic agents for high-risk LUAD. Multilayer gene regulatory network reconstruction and GLMY homology analysis revealed progressive disruption of higher-order immune-regulatory organization from normal to tumor tissues and between low TLS-risk/low ICD-risk (LL-risk) and high TLS-risk/high ICD-risk (HH-risk) states. CONCLUSIONS: TLS- and ICD-related programs jointly delineate clinically significant immune states in LUAD through convergent transcriptomic, genetic, single-cell, spatial, pharmacological, and systems-level evidence, and are associated with immune microenvironment remodeling, immunotherapy responsiveness, prognosis, and therapeutic vulnerability. These findings establish a biomarker-guided, machine learning-supported framework for LUAD risk stratification and may inform more precise immunotherapy-oriented therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pediatric patients who experience firearm injury may be at risk for subsequent reinjury, yet the timing and predictors of recurrence remain poorly defined. Characterizing reinjury patterns at both individual and system levels is essential for informing targeted prevention strategies. METHODS: We performed a retrospective review (2010-2024) of patients aged 0-18 years presenting with non-self-inflicted firearm injuries to two Level I pediatric and adult trauma centers. Cross-institutional database linkage was used to identify reinjury events. Cumulative incidence functions estimated reinjury risk over time, accounting for death as a competing risk. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models evaluated independent predictors of reinjury. RESULTS: Among 834 patients (84.9% male, 79% Black; median age 17 years [IQR 15-18]), 67 died from their index injury and 75 sustained a subsequent firearm injury at a median of 22 months (IQR 12-61). No reinjury events occurred among children younger than 11 years. Cumulative reinjury incidence at one, three, and five years was 2.5% (1.4-3.6), 5.9% (4.2-7.5), and 7.8% (5.8-9.7), respectively. Assault-related index injury (aHR 2.18, 95% CI 1.10-4.35), lower injury severity (aHR 0.59, 95% CI 0.36-0.97), and treatment at an adult trauma center (aHR 3.43, 95% CI 1.46-8.06) were independently associated with increased reinjury risk. CONCLUSIONS: Firearm reinjury among pediatric patients is concentrated in adolescence and often occurs years after the initial event. Reinjured youth were more likely to have been assaulted, uninsured, and initially treated for relatively minor injuries-factors that may limit engagement with supportive services. These findings underscore the need for developmentally tailored violence-prevention and resource-linkage interventions initiated at the time of first injury.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pediatric cervical spine injuries (CSI) are present in 1-2% of all pediatric traumatic injuries and can be devastating. Contemporary injury prevention measures may decrease CSI incidence, however, their impact on pediatric CSI incidence are unknown. We aimed to evaluate contemporary epidemiological data of pediatric CSI in the United States. METHODS: We evaluated the incidence of pediatric CSI using the Trauma Quality Improvement Program (TQIP) database from 2017-2024. Amongst children (age 0-17) with blunt trauma, CSI cases and CSI-related operative interventions were identified using ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS codes, respectively. Trends in the incidence of overall and operative CSI were assessed for the total cohort and across age groups. P<0.05 was defined as statistically significant. RESULTS: Among 805,466 pediatric patients with blunt trauma the overall incidence of CSI was 1.9% (<1 years: 0.5%, 1-4 years: 1.0%, 5-9 years: 0.9%, 10-14 years: 1.7%, 15-17 years: 4.4%). Increasing age and motor vehicle accident mechanism were independently associated with CSI. There was a significant decrease in overall- (2017: 2.08 %, 2024: 1.8%) and operative- (2017: 15.3%, 2024: 12.5%) CSI incidence across the study period, not explained by changes in overall trauma volume. CONCLUSIONS: Among traumatically injured children presenting to trauma centers in the United States, the incidence of CSI is decreasing over time. These findings suggest that public health measures such as improving vehicle safety standards, restraint- and helmet-laws may have a measurable impact on this potentially devastating pediatric injury pattern.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Despite widespread adoption of total urogenital mobilization (TUM) for feminizing genitoplasty in congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), quantitative intraoperative benchmarks remain unreported in the literature, and urinary continence outcomes in CAH remain incompletely established. PURPOSE: To document urinary continence, complication rate and other operative parameters of TUM performed exclusively for CAH in a consecutive single-center cohort. METHODS: 73 consecutive 46,XX CAH patients (Prader III, n=45; Prader IV, n=28), aged 2 to 168 months, underwent TUM at a single institution between January 2014 and March 2025. Operative time, estimated blood loss, complications, and urinary continence, assessed clinically and urodynamically, were analyzed. Spearman correlation assessed the relationship between common channel length and intraoperative parameters. RESULTS: Urinary continence, supported by clinical and urodynamic findings, was preserved in all 52 toilet-trained patients (100%). No complication attributable to the surgical technique occurred over 4 years median follow-up; 11 patients (15.1%) developed catheter-related Grade I urinary tract infection, all resolving fully. Median operative time was 145 minutes (IQR 120-178) and median estimated blood loss was 16 mL (IQR 12-19); no patient required perioperative transfusion. Common channel length correlated strongly with operative time (r=0.83, p<0.001) but not with estimated blood loss (r=0.23, p=0.09). Four patients with common channel length exceeding 6.5 cm required distal urethral plate augmentation without bladder neck involvement. CONCLUSIONS: TUM demonstrates a favorable perioperative and postoperative safety profile in CAH, with hemostatic stability independent of anatomical complexity. TUM safely preserves continence even in older children and anatomically complex cases with appropriate technical modification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Trauma patients frequently have comorbid substance use disorders (SUD), which may complicate pain management and increase the risk of opioid-related adverse outcomes after discharge. We hypothesized that trauma patients with SUD would be prescribed more opioids at discharge than those without SUD. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of adult trauma patients across the state from 2022 to 2025 using a statewide collaborative database. Primary outcomes were opioid prescription at discharge (yes/no) and amount prescribed standardized to oxycodone 5 mg pills. A multivariable approach assessed risk-adjusted differences in outcomes among patients with SUD versus without SUD. RESULTS: Among 29,805 total patients, 8,672 (29.1%) had a diagnosis of SUD. 71.2% of patients with SUD received a discharge opioid prescription, compared with 59.6% of patients without SUD (p<0.001). After adjustment, the predicted probability of receiving an opioid prescription at discharge was 64.2% (95% CI, 63.1%-65.2%) for patients with SUD and 62.5% (95% CI, 62.0%-63.1%) for those without. Among patients that received a prescription, those with SUD were prescribed 21.2 pills of 5 mg oxycodone, corresponding to an adjusted difference of 1.6 additional pills (95% CI, 0.89-2.31; p<0.001) compared with those without. Prescribing patterns also differed by race and ethnicity: Hispanic or Latino patients were 5.4-percentage points more likely to receive an opioid prescription than non-Hispanic or Latino patients, while, among prescription recipients, Black patients received 3.56 fewer pills than White patients. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that patients with SUD received opioids more frequently and in greater amounts at discharge, yet absolute differences were small in magnitude and may not represent clinically meaningful differences. Differences in prescribing by race and ethnicity were larger in magnitude and warrant further investigation. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic and epidemiological; Level III.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) is the most common intracranial injury in mild TBI (mTBI), particularly in older adults. However, the relationship of patient and brain computed tomography (CT) characteristics with outcomes remains poorly described in a contemporary cohort. This study aims to characterize outcomes in younger and older adults with mTBI and isolated acute SDH. METHODS: This was a 10-center, retrospective cohort study of adult traumas with emergency department Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 13 to 15 and acute traumatic SDH on initial brain CT ('22-'23). Trauma registry, EHR, and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) data were collected through automated and manual methods. The primary outcome was total mortality (TM=death+hospice discharge); the sample was stratified by 18 to 64 versus older than or equal to 65 years. Multivariable backward selection logistic regression examined 21 demographic, injury, and brain CT covariates. RESULTS: In total, 1,157 patients were included (18-64 y: 28%; ≥65 y: 72%; 58% transferred in). Median [IQR] non-head ISS was 1 [1-5] in 18 to 64 years, and 1 [1-2] in older than or equal to 65 years. Ten percent had neurosurgical intervention (18-64 y: 8%; ≥65 y: 11%). TM was higher in older than or equal to 65 years than 18 to 64 years (10% vs. 3%). Compared with older than or equal to 65 years, 18 to 64 years were discharged home more frequently (78% vs. 51%) and to hospice less frequently (2% vs. 7%). In 18 to 64 years, factors associated with TM were race, advance directive, functional dependence, ISS, more midline shift, and thicker SDH (too few TMs for adjusted models). In older than or equal to 65 years, factors independently associated with TM were advance directive (aOR [95% CI]: 11.8 [2.9-49.0]), male sex (3.0 [1.3-7.0]), midline shift (1.8 [1.3-2.6]), shock index (1.5 [1.1-2.1]), and worsening SDH on follow-up CT (2.9 [1.3-6.6]). CONCLUSIONS: Despite presenting as "mild", these data highlight that older adults with SDH have high TM and should continue to receive the highest-level care with timely goals-of-care discussions. The association between advance directives and TM should be interpreted within the context of baseline vulnerability and preinjury treatment preferences, not as a biological mortality predictor. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) often requires repeat head computed tomography (CT) imaging to monitor for bleed progression. While prior literature has explored patient-level factors, data on the impact of ICH morphologies (subdural [SDH], epidural [EDH], intraparenchymal [IPH], intraventricular [IVH], and multicompartment hemorrhage [MCH]) on radiographic ICH progression remains unclear. We hypothesized that MCH and IVH would have an increased associated risk of progression. METHODS: This retrospective (2021-2023) single-center cohort included adults (≥18 y) with TBI-related ICH who underwent initial and repeat head CT. Patients were stratified into radiographic progression versus no-progression cohorts, with progression defined as new or enlarging hemorrhage on attending radiologist interpretation of follow-up head CT. The primary outcome was the rate of radiographic progression for each ICH type. MCH was defined as the presence of two or more ICH types. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between each ICH type and radiographic progression, adjusting for age, mechanism of injury, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival, trauma-bay intubation, and preinjury antithrombotic exposure. RESULTS: Of the 817 patients with ICH on initial head CT and documented repeat CT, 401 (49.1%) had radiographic progression. Patients with progression were younger (58 vs. 62 y, p=0.027), more frequently male (71.3% vs. 63.7%, p=0.020), and had similar antithrombotic exposure (15.2% vs. 14.2%, p=0.678). Craniotomy/craniectomy was more frequent among those with progression (21.2% vs. 8.2%, p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, MCH demonstrated the strongest associated risk for progression (odds ratio [OR] 5.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.36-9.33, p<0.001), whereas IPH (OR 2.02, CI: 0.86-4.75, p=0.108), SDH, EDH, and IVH were not independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. CONCLUSIONS: MCH was independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. This higher-risk hemorrhage pattern may warrant closer neurological monitoring. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Globally, rising drug-resistant urinary tract infections (UTIs) affect older populations disproportionally. We aimed to assess the incidence, management, and patient outcomes of UTIs in English care homes. METHODS: Using linked primary, secondary, social care, and pathology data covering 2·5 million patients in London between 2018 and 2023, we matched older adults with UTIs living in care homes with older adults living outside care homes using propensity scores. We performed a time-series analysis of incidence and compared urine culture turnaround time and results (including antimicrobial resistance). We assessed UTI-related patient outcomes, including death, complications, recurrent infection, and antibiotic re-prescription within 60 days, using generalised estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and other risk factors. FINDINGS: We identified 91 501 UTI cases, including 6648 (7·3%) in care homes. In care homes, 4678 (70·4%) of the 6448 UTIs occurred in women and 3779 (56·8%) involved individuals aged 85 years or older. The older adults living in care homes were older (median age: 86 years [IQR 80-91] vs 76 years [71-83]) and more frequently White (70·3% vs 56·7%) than older adults living outside care homes. The incidence rate of community-acquired UTIs was 1909·4 per 100 000 person-months in care homes (increasing by 3·7 [95% CI 0·8-6·6] per month), as compared with 543·5 outside care homes (decreasing by 1·3 [-1·8 to -0·7] per month). Urine cultures were used less (1366 [20·5%] of 6648 [95% CI 19·6-21·5] vs 24 699 [29·1%] of 84 853 [28·8-29·4]), were more likely to be polymicrobial (suggesting contamination; 416 [30·4%] of 1366 [28·1-32·9] vs 4325 [17·5%] of 24 699 [17·0-18·0]), and had a longer turnaround time (52·9% turnaround in 1 day [50·3-55·6] vs 66·2% [65·6-66·8]) in care homes than outside care homes. Escherichia coli UTIs had higher resistance to trimethoprim (46·4% [95% CI 41·0-51·9] vs 32·0% [30·9-33·1]) and nitrofurantoin (7·5% [4·9-10·8] vs 2·4% [2·0-2·8]) in care homes than outside care homes. Care home cases had significantly worse 60-day outcomes, with higher risk of death (1·99 [95% CI 1·67-2·36]; p<0·001), presenting to general practitioners (1·38 [1·01-1·89]; p=0·042) and to hospitals (1·15 [1·01-1·32]; p=0·041) with complications, recurrent infections (1·22 [1·08-1·36]; p=0·001), and antibiotic re-prescription (1·11 [1·01-1·21]; p=0·024). INTERPRETATION: Older adults residing in care homes had higher UTI infection burden and worse clinical outcomes than matched older adults residing outside care homes. Possible explanatory factors include inadequate care, discordant prescribing decisions, and disconnect with diagnostic capabilities, in addition to the exacerbating effects on infection management during the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings highlight the need for improvement in infection management in care home settings. FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research; Wellcome Trust; Fleming Initiative.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: During Brazil's unprecedented dengue epidemic in 2023-2025, we develop a rationale for organ donor screening to mitigate the risk of donor derived transmission using rapid, widely available, and low-cost tests. Here we aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and outcomes among kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) who developed different routes of dengue infection and establish a policy for mitigating the risk of donor transmission. METHODS: This study conducted at a large kidney transplant center in Brazil-Hospital do Rim (HRIM) examined dengue in KTRs through three components: initial cases of donor-derived infection that led to systematic donor screening; donor screening and adjudication for potential transmission from August 2023 to April 2025; and outcomes of vector-borne dengue among recipients followed at HRIM from December 2023 to July 2024. Donors were screened using immunochromatographic NS1 antigen and IgM rapid tests, with RT-PCR for those NS1-negative and IgM-positive. FINDINGS: Before August 2023, we recorded four donor-derived transmissions from two deceased donors, resulting in three deaths. After that, among 1252 deceased donors screened, eight were NS1-positive and four had clinical evidence of dengue; these 12 donors were excluded from donation. Among 58 NS1-negative/IgM-positive donors, 38 were considered for donation. From these, 52 recipients were transplanted, with no confirmed donor-derived transmission. Among 1542 recipients of kidneys from NS1- and IgM-negative donors, 17 developed dengue within 30 days after transplantation: one had fatal transfusion-transmitted dengue, two had confirmed donor-derived transmission, ten had potential donor-derived transmission, and four were considered to have vector-borne infection acquired before transplantation. Every recipient with confirmed or potential donor-derived transmission identified during the screened period recovered from the infection. Lastly, among 12,402 KTRs on follow-up, we recorded 373 confirmed vector-borne cases. They were 50·0 years old, 203 were male (54·4%), 170 were female (45·6%), and 232 were White (62·2%). The case-fatality rate was 1·88%, compared with 0·10% in the general population during the same period. INTERPRETATION: KTRs with vector-borne dengue experienced a high observed case-fatality rate. Organ or blood transmission led to life-threatening outcomes. The rapid test screening was associated with low transmission, and when it occurred, the risk of severe cases was mitigated. These findings support the incorporation of dengue screening strategies in endemic regions. FUNDING: Fundação Oswaldo Ramos.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To externally validate and update a published normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model for the prediction of Grade ≥ 2 acute oesophageal toxicity (AOT) in lung cancer patients receiving (chemo-)radiotherapy (predictors: concurrent chemotherapy, gender, tumour stage, mean oesophagus dose (MOD)). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patient cohorts from four centres were available. Initial external validation was performed by assessing model performance. Heterogeneity of performance across cohorts was evaluated using an internal-external cross validation (IECV) method. Based on the IECV procedure, parameters were added or removed from the model to lower heterogeneity in model performance across cohorts with the aim to create a model that performed uniformly well across centres. Ridge regression was used to create the final model and bootstrapping techniques were applied to perform further internal validation. RESULTS: Out of 937 patients, 444 (47%) had Grade ≥ 2 AOT. External validation indicated model recalibration was necessary for 1 cohort and model revision for another. IECV showed heterogeneity of performance of the original model across cohorts. To lower heterogeneity in model performance, the predictors concurrent chemotherapy, gender, and tumour stage were removed from the model, and overall treatment time (OTT) was added. The final model containing MOD and OTT as predictors showed low levels of heterogeneity in model performance (I2 of 0% for all performance measures) with optimism-corrected AUC of 0.75, calibration intercept of -0.01 and slope of 1.26. CONCLUSION: The validation and updating of an NTCP-model for AOT resulted in a prediction model performing well in varying patient cohorts. Therefore, this updated model was added to the national indication protocol to select lung cancer patients for proton radiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Whether technical difficulty influences outcomes after transanal total mesorectal excision (TaTME) for middle and low rectal cancer remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between technical difficulty and patient outcomes. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 210 consecutive patients with middle and low rectal cancer who underwent TaTME at three centers in China. A five-item technical difficulty score was constructed using male sex, body mass index ≥ 25 kg/m2, distance from the anal verge ≤5 cm, tumor diameter ≥ 4 cm, and neoadjuvant therapy. Patients were classified into low (0-2 points) and high (3-5 points) technical difficulty groups. Surgical outcomes, recurrence patterns, disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and conditional survival were compared. RESULTS: Overall, 130 patients were classified into the low technical difficulty group and 80 into the high technical difficulty group. The high technical difficulty group had a longer operative time (249.0 ± 60.0 vs. 220.3 ± 50.1 min, P < 0.001), but major short-term outcomes did not differ significantly. The 3-year DFS and OS rates were 80.2% and 89.0%, respectively. Forty postoperative recurrences were recorded, mainly distant metastases, with most occurring within 2 years. Overall recurrence (17.7% vs. 21.2%, P = 0.588) and local recurrence (3.8% vs. 2.5%, P = 0.711) were comparable between groups. High technical difficulty was not independently associated with DFS (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.57-2.00, P = 0.849) or OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 0.52-2.81, P = 0.664). CONCLUSION: Technical difficulty in TaTME was mainly reflected by prolonged operative time and was not significantly associated with increased local recurrence or reduced 3-year DFS/OS. Early surveillance for systemic recurrence remains important.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided gallbladder drainage (EUS-GBD) has emerged as a potential alternative to endoscopic ultrasound-guided choledochoduodenostomy (EUS-CD) for distal malignant biliary obstruction (DMBO) after failed endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP). Comparative evidence remains scarce. METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients who underwent EUS-GBD or EUS-CD using electrocautery-enhanced lumen-apposing metal stents after failed ERCP at four Spanish tertiary centers. The primary outcome was clinical success, defined as a ≥50% reduction in serum bilirubin within one week or normalization (< 2 mg/dL) within one month. Secondary outcomes included technical success, adverse events, endoscopic reintervention, hospital stay, and mortality. RESULTS: Sixty patients were included, with 35 undergoing EUS-GBD and 25 EUS-CD. Baseline characteristics were comparable except for older age in the EUS-CD group (79.8 vs. 71.7 years; p = 0.01). Clinical success was achieved in 74.3% and 88.0% of patients, respectively (p = 0.33), while technical success was 100% and 96.0% (p = 0.40). Bilirubin reduction at 24 h, 48 h, 7, 14, and 30 days and median hospital stay were similar. Adverse events occurred in 20.0% in the EUS-CD group and 37.2% of patients in the EUS-GBD group (p = 0.25), and reintervention rates were 12.0%, and 28.6%, respectively (p = 0.20). Thirty-day mortality and overall survival did not differ significantly. Seven patients undergoing EUS-GBD subsequently underwent pancreatoduodenectomy without complications related to LAMS. CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with DMBO after failed ERCP, EUS-GBD provides efficacy and safety comparable to EUS-CD and represents a feasible rescue option when choledochoduodenostomy is technically challenging or not feasible.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Delayed gastric conduit emptying (DGCE) is common in patients following esophagectomy, and its treatment remains challenging. This study evaluated efficacy and safety of gastric peroral endoscopic pyloromyotomy (GPOEM) and predictors of treatment response. METHODS: We prospectively included patients with symptoms of DGCE following esophagectomy scheduled for GPOEM in two tertiary referral centers. EndoFLIP measurements were conducted before and 3 months after GPOEM. Gastric emptying scintigraphy (GES) was performed prior to, 3 and 12 months after GPOEM. Efficacy was evaluated by clinical success, defined as a score of 1 or 2 on a six-point Likert scale 3 months after GPOEM. Predictive factors for clinical success, including pyloric distensibility, GES and response to prior pylorus-directed therapy (botulinum injection and pyloric dilatation), were evaluated by exploratory analyses. RESULTS: The technical success rate of GPOEM was 95% (19/20; 95% CI 75-100). At 3-, and 12-months post-procedure, the clinical success rates were 68% (13/19; 95% CI 37-84) and 44% (8/18; 95% CI 22-67). Distensibility prior to GPOEM did not differ significantly between patients with and without clinical success (3.7 vs. 4.0 mm2/mmHg, p = 0.70). Pre-GPOEM 4-h gastric retention was greater in patients with clinical success than those without, but this was not significant (33 vs 16%, p = 0.12). Although there was no significant association between prior response to pylorus-directed therapy and GPOEM success (p = 0.10), the positive and negative predictive value were 100% (9/9; 95% CI 66-100) and 40% (2/5; 95% CI 5-85). CONCLUSION: GPOEM is feasible and safe in patients with DGCE following esophagectomy, demonstrating initial efficacy in two-thirds of patients, although this declined to less than half at 1-year follow-up. In exploratory analyses, no predictors of treatment response were identified. Larger studies are needed to investigate if response to pylorus-directed therapy may predict an increased likelihood of treatment response.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but can disrupt ocular immune privilege and produce heterogeneous immune-related adverse events (Eye-irAEs). This structured narrative review with evidence mapping integrates clinical, epidemiologic, mechanistic, pharmacovigilance, and management data to define translational pathways from checkpoint blockade to ocular toxicity and treatment decisions. In a real-world cohort of 41,020 ICI-treated patients, ophthalmic irAEs occurred in 4.18% within 1 year, including dry eye disease in 2.00%, conjunctivitis in 0.87%, blepharitis in 0.51%, anterior uveitis in 0.39%, and keratitis in 0.38%. A 2026 meta-analysis of five cohorts comprising 277,790 participants found increased uveitis risk with ICI exposure (hazard ratio 2.26), while pooled overall survival was not significantly associated with ICI-related uveitis (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.35-1.39). Among patients with preexisting uveitis, recurrence reached 38.9% for prior anterior disease and 51.1% for prior intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis. Risk varies by malignancy and regimen; melanoma was associated with substantially greater noninfectious uveitis than lung cancer (1.10% vs 0.18%; risk ratio 6.17, 95% CI 4.20-9.08). Mechanistically, PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4 have the strongest established exposure-toxicity evidence, LAG-3 signals are emerging, and TIM-3 and TIGIT remain translational. Phenotype-directed local or systemic therapy can preserve vision and permit ICI continuation or rechallenge in selected patients. In a 2026 rechallenge series, four of five rechallenged patients had no documented recurrence, while one recurrence resolved successfully with corticosteroid treatment. Standardized phenotyping, longitudinal ophthalmic surveillance, multidisciplinary attribution, and prospective ocular endpoints should translate mechanistic insight into safer immunotherapy, individualized rechallenge, and improved cancer-treatment continuity.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Randomised trials indicate that early integration of specialised palliative care improves quality of life and, in some studies, survival in advanced cancer, yet its implementation in inpatient oncology remains inconsistent. This study quantifies the coded utilisation of specialised inpatient palliative care in German hospitals and interprets adoption patterns using the diffusion of innovations theory. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of nationwide hospital cases reimbursed under the German diagnosis-related groups (DRG) system in 2023. The analysis included the most common solid malignancies and assessed the utilisation of specialised inpatient palliative care overall and stratified by metastatic status, tumour entity, comorbidities, and treating medical specialties. Results: Specialised inpatient palliative care was provided in 5.4% of hospital cases involving the most common malignant tumours. Among patients with organ metastases, utilisation increased to a median rate of 15.0% of hospital cases, with the highest rates observed in cases with brain (17.8%), bone (17.0%), and pleural metastases (16.1%). Palliative care involvement correlated positively with in-hospital mortality. Interpreted cautiously through the diffusion of innovations theory, which frames the 15 to 20% band as a heuristic landmark rather than a validated threshold, utilisation even in the metastatic subgroup reaches only the lower edge of this band, indicating that uptake remains confined to innovators and early adopters and has not extended to the early majority. Conclusions: Specialised inpatient palliative care remains underutilised in German oncology, reaching 5.4% of all cases and a median of 15.0% even in metastatic disease. Interpreted cautiously through the diffusion of innovations theory, which frames the 15 to 20% band as a heuristic landmark, uptake appears confined to early adopters and has not yet reached the early majority.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Patients with high-grade glioma (HGG) have a poor prognosis despite maximal safe resection, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, partly because of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Unfortunately, all phase III trials of anti-PD-1 therapy to date have failed to yield positive results in HGGs. Recent early-phase trials have identified promising strategies involving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Here, we share our 8-year experience with anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with HGG in a real-world setting. Methods: All patients with HGG who received PD-1 inhibitor-based therapy at our center between 2018 and 2026 were included. Medical records were reviewed longitudinally for each patient, and the latest follow-up data were collected. Patients lost to follow-up were excluded. Results: Four regimens involving anti-PD-1 treatment were identified in 22 patients with HGG (newly diagnosed = 11, recurrent = 11): (1) VEGFR-targeted therapy plus PD-1 inhibition (9 recurrent HGGs), (2) the "2-THE-TOP" regimen (tumor-treating fields plus temozolomide and PD-1 inhibitor therapy) (5 newly diagnosed HGGs), (3) anti-PD-1 monotherapy (2 recurrent and 2 newly diagnosed HGGs), and (4) neoadjuvant plus adjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy (4 newly diagnosed HGGs). Median overall survival for these four regimens was 32.7, 20.3, 28.6, and 31.8 months, respectively. No grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were recorded. Conclusions: Our preliminary observations suggest that PD-1 blockade may remain a viable option for patients with HGG when combined with specific therapies, administered with careful timing, and applied in selected patients.

papers.abstract_en: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are central orchestrators of immune evasion, therapeutic resistance, and clinical outcome across diverse solid tumors. However, the classical M1/M2 paradigm fails to capture the lineage diversity, spatial heterogeneity, and functional plasticity of TAMs within the tumor microenvironment. Unlike previous reviews that mainly summarize macrophage polarization or TAM subtype classification, this review focuses on how emerging single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies redefine TAM ontogeny, phenotypic diversity, spatial organization, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. This review summarizes how fate-mapping, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial multi-omics have contributed to the understanding of the dual origins of TAMs, including embryo-derived tissue-resident macrophages and monocyte-derived macrophages, and how these technologies further delineate transcriptionally and functionally distinct TAM subsets such as SPP1+, TREM2+, C1QC+, and MMP9+ TAMs with context-dependent roles in immune regulation, metastasis, and treatment resistance. We then integrate spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging, and radiomics evidence to outline TAM-enriched niches at hypoxic cores, invasive fronts, perivascular regions and tertiary lymphoid structures, emphasizing how these niches coordinate crosstalk among cancer cells, T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, endothelial cells and B cells. Emerging TAM-related gene signatures and multi-omics-based scores were further highlighted that predict response or resistance to radiotherapy, chemotherapy, anti-angiogenic therapy, and immune checkpoint blockade. Finally, we provide a forward-looking perspective on strategies to reprogram, deplete, or redirect specific TAM subsets, including CSF1/CSF1R and CCR2/CCL2 blockade, metabolic and epigenetic modulators, agonists of phagocytosis, and CAR-macrophage-based therapies. Overall, we propose that integrating single-cell and spatial omics with AI-assisted digital pathology and longitudinal sampling will enable TAM-informed patient stratification and rational design of combination immunotherapies, thereby accelerating the translation of TAM biology into precision oncology.

papers.abstract_en: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a devastating form of central nervous system (CNS) dissemination in lung cancer, particularly non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Current treatment frameworks emphasize CNS drug penetration, oncogenic driver evolution, and intrathecal therapy. Emerging evidence supports viewing the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) compartment as an active tumor-immune space, but the field remains early, with limited lung cancer-specific mechanistic and single-cell datasets. Lung cancer cells in CSF appear to adapt to low protein content, limited nutrients, fluid shear, weak matrix support, and compartmental immune surveillance. Meanwhile, available CSF studies suggest immune states marked by exhausted T cells, regulatory lymphoid programs, suppressive myeloid remodeling, cytokine dysregulation, and tumor-supportive signaling. This review summarizes the CSF metastatic niche, tumor adaptation, immune-cell states, tumor-immune crosstalk, therapy-associated remodeling, and CSF multi-omics in lung cancer LM. We propose that CSF-guided profiling may help generate immune-state classifications and inform future targeted, intrathecal, immune, or combination strategies, while requiring prospective validation before routine treatment guidance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in the United States. Individual-level risk factors such as tobacco use are well characterized, but the community-level environmental, social, and economic contributions to geographic variation in incidence remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We conducted an ecological analysis of 542 Medical Service Study Areas (MSSAs) in California, linking age-adjusted lung cancer incidence rates (AAIR, 2015-2019) to 27 indicators of pollution, population characteristics, and adult smoking prevalence. Machine learning and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) distinguished high- versus low-incidence MSSAs; ordinary least squares (OLS) regression quantified covariate-AAIR associations. RESULTS: A Support Vector Machine (radial basis function kernel) trained on 15 autoencoder-selected indicators discriminated best (cross-validation AUC = 0.891), outperforming a smoking-only model (AUC = 0.685). By SHAP, smoking, linguistic isolation, neighborhood SES, unemployment, and housing burden contributed most. In OLS regression, neighborhood SES quintile (standardized β = -0.57) and Hispanic population proportion (β = -0.51) were the strongest predictors of lower AAIR; higher Black population proportion was associated with higher AAIR. Subpopulation-stratified models performed better for White-specific (AUC = 0.926) than Hispanic-specific AAIR (AUC = 0.744). CONCLUSIONS: Community-level smoking, pollution, and population characteristics data improved the identification of regions with elevated lung cancer risk. IMPACT: Community-level indicators can identify areas of elevated lung cancer burden, including the many where registry rates are suppressed. These associations are concurrent rather than etiologic, and no causal interpretation is intended. Lower predictive performance in some subpopulations highlights data gaps that must be addressed for equitable cancer prevention.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Persistent lung cancer mortality despite screening is multifactorial. Characterizing computed tomography (CT) findings preceding fatal lung cancer may identify imaging features and screening challenges that warrant further study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, outcome-enriched case series nested within the 26,722-participant low-dose computed tomography arm of the National Lung Screening Trial. Among 359 participants who died of lung cancer within the prespecified interval, exclusions for positive baseline screening (n = 186), incomplete screening (n = 28), withdrawal/declined screening (n = 19), unavailable CTs (n = 6), or three negative screens followed by death 2+ years after the final screen (n = 29) yielded 91 participants. Screening CTs were retrospectively assessed using the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) v2022. Four thoracic radiologists independently reviewed visible-in-retrospect nodules and adjudicated whether they met criteria for suspicion. RESULTS: Of 91 participants, 22 (24%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 17%-34%) had visible-in-retrospect nodules considered suspicious under Lung-RADS v2022 ("missed"), 16 (18%; 95% CI, 11%-27%) had visible nodules not meeting suspicion criteria ("not callable"), 50 (55%; 95% CI, 45%-65%) had no visible-in-retrospect nodule, and 3 (3.3%) were inconclusive. Missed nodules were frequently juxtapleural (41%), obscured (50%), or irregularly bordered (68%); not-callable nodules were frequently <6 mm (75%), juxtapleural (56%), or irregularly bordered (56%). CONCLUSION: In this selected fatal-case series, small and juxtapleural nodules were common among visible nodules not meeting Lung-RADS v2022 suspicion criteria. These findings warrant evaluation in representative screening populations and should not be interpreted as estimates of population-level Lung-RADS performance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of exocrine glands, including minor salivary glands (MSG), with potential formation of ectopic germinal centers. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are critical suppressors of autoimmune responses, and their dysfunction has been implicated in SjD pathogenesis. FoxP3, the master transcription factor of Tregs, undergoes alternative splicing to produce four variants: full-length (FL), Δ2, Δ7, and Δ2Δ7. While FoxP3 splice variants are known to influence Treg proliferation and suppressive activity, their profile and functional significance in Tregs from SjD patients remain poorly characterized. METHODS: Peripheral blood was collected from 20 SjD patients or 20 healthy donors (HD). MSG biopsies were obtained from 10 SjD patients. Tregs were isolated from blood and biopsy tissue by immunomagnetic separation and expanded ex vivo. FoxP3 splice variant mRNA levels were quantified by real-time RT-PCR. Treg phenotype (CD4, CD25, CD127, CD152, Helios), suppressive molecules (CD39, CD223, granzymes A/B, perforin), was assessed by flow cytometry. The concentrations of suppressive cytokines IL-10 andIL-35 were accessed by Bio-Plex assay. Proliferation was evaluated by cell counting. Suppressive activity was determined by mixed lymphocyte reaction. Splice-switching oligonucleotides (SSOs) were used to induce Δ7 FoxP3 expression to confirm direct functional effects. RESULTS: Peripheral blood Tregs from SjD patients showed significantly decreased increased Δ7 FoxP3 splice variant compared to HD. MSG-derived Tregs from SjD patients also predominantly expressed the Δ7 FoxP3 variant. High-expressing Δ7 FoxP3 Tregs exhibited reduced proliferative activity, division frequency and decreased suppressive activity compared to low-expressing Δ7 FoxP3 Tregs. High-expressing Δ7 FoxP3 Tregs showed significantly reduced CD127low and Helios expression, decreased CD39, CD223, granzyme, and granzyme B. IL-10 and IL-35 production was also reduced. SSO-mediated induction of Δ7 FoxP3 MSG-derived Tregs confirmed these phenotypic and functional changes. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that elevated Δ7 FoxP3 splice variant expression in MSG-derived Tregs from SjD patients is associated with impaired proliferative and suppressive function, reduced expression of suppressive molecules and cytokines, and a phenotype suggestive of a transitional or immature Treg state. The results highlight the functional consequences of altered FoxP3 alternative splicing in SjD pathogenesis and suggest a possible involvement of Tregs in the biology of ectopic germinal centers in SjD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Macrophages sense viral double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) via the innate immune receptors TLR3 and MDA5 whose activation drives a robust inflammatory program, often coupled to cell death. TLR3/TRIF-dependent apoptosis has been described in response to dsRNA. Growing evidence suggests that dsRNA may trigger multiple forms of cell death with mechanisms yet to be elucidated. In addition to TLR/TRIF axis, the necroptosis regulator RIPK3 has been implicated in both inflammatory response and cell death during viral infections in several cell types. However, its role in regulating these two events in human macrophages remains unclear. METHODS: Here, we investigated in human monocyte-derived macrophages (hMDMs) the mechanisms of dsRNA induced cell death and its temporal and molecular linkage to inflammatory signaling, with a focus on the interplay between RIPK3 and the TLR3/TRIF pathways. RESULTS: We found that intracellular Poly(I:C), a synthetic analogue of dsRNA, induced cell death with apoptotic and necroptotic features. TRIF-mediated signaling cascade and RIPK3 jointly contributed to caspase-8 activation leading to apoptosis. RIPK3 also promoted necroptosis by inducing MLKL phosphorylation. Downstream of caspases, Poly(I:C) induced cleavage of Gasdermin E (GSDME), which remained intracellular and localized in mitochondria contributing to the amplification of caspase-3 activation. RIPK3-dependent signaling drove the release of IFN-β and TNF-α and promoted the upregulation of the sensors TLR3 and MDA5, thereby amplifying the inflammatory axis. The inflammatory response preceded cell death, with RIPK3 being the key regulator of the early signaling and TLR3/TRIF becoming involved at later timepoints. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings identify RIPK3 as key mediator coordinating dsRNA-induced inflammatory signaling and regulated cell death in human macrophages.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer is a highly aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis, and its molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood, with effective therapeutic options still limited. Establishment of sister chromatid cohesion N-acetyltransferase 1 (ESCO1) has been implicated in the development and progression of several malignancies; however, its biological role and underlying mechanisms in pancreatic cancer remain largely unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the clinical significance and molecular mechanisms of the ESCO1/NUFIP2 axis in pancreatic cancer. METHODS: TCGA, CPTAC, and other publicly available datasets were used to evaluate the expression patterns, diagnostic value, and prognostic significance of ESCO1 and NUFIP2 in pancreatic cancer. In vitro and in vivo experiments were subsequently performed to characterize the biological functions of the ESCO1/NUFIP2 axis and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: ESCO1 and NUFIP2 were significantly upregulated in pancreatic cancer and were associated with poor prognosis. Functional assays demonstrated that the ESCO1/NUFIP2 axis promoted pancreatic cancer cell proliferation and migration, enhanced tumor growth in vivo, and suppressed apoptosis. Mechanistically, ESCO1 promoted NUFIP2 acetylation and limited its K48-linked ubiquitination and subsequent degradation, thereby maintaining NUFIP2 protein stability. Stabilized NUFIP2 preserved mitochondrial function and suppressed mitochondrial apoptosis, whereas NUFIP2 overexpression or trichostatin A (TSA) treatment partially reversed the effects of ESCO1 depletion. Moreover, the ESCO1/NUFIP2 axis was associated with immune cell infiltration, and depletion of either ESCO1 or NUFIP2 enhanced dendritic cell (DC)-mediated cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) antitumor responses. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) and osteoporosis (OP) frequently coexist, but their shared inflammatory molecular features remain unclear. We investigated whether the two disorders share an immune-extracellular matrix axis and sought candidate inflammation-associated biomarkers. METHODS: Public transcriptomic datasets GSE124272 and GSE35956 were analyzed separately using differential expression analysis and gene set enrichment analysis. Shared genes were prioritized using LASSO regression, random forest, and support vector machine algorithms, with model performance estimated by nested stratified cross-validation. Exploratory nomograms, network pharmacology, and molecular docking were performed. Expression of NCF2, CRH, and BTK was examined in TNF-α-stimulated immortalized human nucleus pulposus cells and osteoblasts. RESULTS: Twenty shared differentially expressed genes were identified, with enrichment patterns involving immune, inflammatory, and metabolic processes. The candidate panel comprised BTK, NCF2, CRH, FCGR3A, and SERPINA3. Nested cross-validation yielded AUCs of 0.86 (95% CI, 0.78-0.93) for IDD and 0.84 (95% CI, 0.75-0.91) for OP. The nomograms were retained as theoretical classification models. TNF-α exposure increased NCF2 and decreased CRH expression in both cell models, while BTK fluorescence increased in nucleus pulposus cells. Docking generated exploratory compound-target predictions after relevance and safety screening. CONCLUSIONS: The analyses identified candidate inflammation-associated molecular signatures shared by the two disorders. The cellular experiments demonstrated responsiveness to acute TNF-α exposure but did not establish biomarker function or disease causality. Independent clinical cohorts, primary cells from multiple donors, functional studies, and direct compound-target validation are required.

papers.abstract_en: Platelet Factor 4 (PF4), a cationic antimicrobial peptide, serves as a ligand for the myeloid-specific phagocytic receptor CR3 (Mac-1, CD11b/CD18). We previously demonstrated that recombinant dimeric PF4 (rPF4) functions as a bacterial opsonin, enhancing phagocytosis of Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and facilitating clearance of both antibiotic-susceptible and methicillin-resistant S. aureus in a mouse model of infectious peritonitis. In this study, we examined whether rPF4 is pathogen-agnostic by assessing its effect on phagocytosis of Gram-negative encapsulated Klebsiella pneumoniae, a WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogen. We demonstrate that rPF4 enhances CR3-mediated phagocytosis of both live and heat-inactivated high-virulence K2 and low-virulence K3 strains of K. pneumoniae by various mouse and human macrophage cell lines, as well as primary neutrophils and macrophages. It also increased phagocytosis of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae. rPF4 did not directly kill bacteria but acted as an opsonin, binding to the negatively charged bacterial capsule and creating recognition sites for CR3 on leukocytes. In a mouse sepsis model, a single dose of rPF4 significantly enhanced bacterial clearance from the lungs, liver, and peritoneum and reduced bacteremia. Histological analyses showed that rPF4 provided substantial protection to lung and liver tissues against K. pneumoniae-induced damage. Consistent with these findings, rPF4 treatment increased the survival rates of infected mice. These results show that rPF4 effectively targets the capsule, a key virulence factor of K. pneumoniae, thereby reducing the bacterium's ability to evade the host immune response. Overall, the data suggest a common mechanism in which cationic rPF4, by binding to the negatively charged surfaces of both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, diminishes their antiphagocytic properties.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: ABO subtypes are characterized by attenuated antigen expression, rendering them susceptible to serological misclassification and posing substantial risks to transfusion safety. Splice-site variants represent one of the mechanisms underlying ABO subtype formation; however, previous mechanistic investigations have predominantly focused on the 5' splice-site(5'SS), leaving the functional consequences of 3' splice-site (3'SS) variants largely unexplored. METHODS: Serological phenotyping of a proband with ABO grouping discrepancy was performed using tube agglutination, microcolumn gel agglutination, and absorption-elution assays. Genotyping was resolved by long-range PCR coupled with Nanopore sequencing. The splicing impact of this novel variant and two previously reported variants, c.29-3C>G and c.29-10T>A, was predicted in silico and validated by in vitro minigene assay. Computational saturation mutagenesis was further deployed to systematically delineate a preliminary framework of regulatory principles governing 3'SS variation. RESULTS: A novel 3'SS variant, c.29-2A>G, was identified in an ABO*A1.02 background in a proband with an Ael phenotype. This novel variant and two previously reported variants disrupted the canonical 3'SS of intron 1, converging on exon 2 skipping as the predominant aberrant splicing event. Additionally, c.29-10T>A activated a cryptic acceptor site, generating a secondary transcript with an 8-bp intronic retention. All aberrant transcripts disrupt the open reading frame and introduce premature termination codons. Through computational saturation mutagenesis, we further established an initial position- and base-dependent risk stratification model for 3'SS variants. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first direct mechanistic evidence linking ABO 3'SS variants to subtype pathogenesis, demonstrating that exon 2 skipping constitutes a shared molecular lesion across intron 1 3'SS variants, ultimately leading to attenuated blood group antigen expression. The preliminary computationally derived risk stratification framework established herein offers a clinically valuable reference for interpreting 3'SS variants, with implications that extend beyond blood group genetics to the broader landscape of splicing-mediated human diseases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In systemic inflammatory diseases, thrombotic complications often cannot be fully explained by traditional risk factors, suggesting that the immune system directly affects hemostasis. The complement system, particularly C1q (the recognition molecule of the classical complement pathway), has been shown to enhance primary hemostasis in vivo and to bind von Willebrand factor (vWF) in vitro. AIM: To investigate the role of the C1q-vWF interaction in human primary hemostasis. METHODS: We used a microfluidic bleeding model with endothelialized microchannels to visualize hemostatic processes in real-time. Following mechanical vessel injury, we tracked C1q deposition and its colocalization with vWF, platelets, and fibrinogen using confocal microscopy. The functional relevance of C1q was assessed using the C1q-inhibitory peptide 2J. RESULTS: C1q accumulates immediately at the injury site and exhibits strong colocalization with vWF and activated platelets, while colocalization with fibrinogen is minimal. Inhibiting C1q with peptide 2J significantly reduces both C1q and vWF deposition during early clot formation, and leads to prolonged bleeding time in this model. CONCLUSION: Deposited C1q functions as a binding partner for vWF, enhancing primary hemostasis. This C1q-vWF axis may contribute to inflammation-related thromboembolic complications in humans.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: 5-Aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) is a first-line therapy for ulcerative colitis, but whether dosing timing influences its therapeutic efficacy remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the chronopharmacological effects of 5-ASA in experimental colitis. METHODS: A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model was used to compare the therapeutic effects of 5-ASA administered at different Zeitgeber times. Colonic proteomic profiling was performed to identify circadian-responsive proteins associated with differential drug efficacy. Intestinal epithelial-specific Bmal1 knockout mice were used to determine whether the circadian clock regulates the chronopharmacological response to 5-ASA. RESULTS: 5-ASA showed marked time-dependent efficacy in DSS-induced colitis, with greater protection at ZT14 than at ZT2. Proteomic analysis identified ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) as a circadian-responsive protein associated with differential treatment outcomes. 5-ASA suppressed FTH1 expression, whereas FTH1 overexpression attenuated anti-inflammatory effects of 5-ASA. Moreover, intestinal epithelial-specific deletion of Bmal1 largely abolished diurnal variation in both FTH1 expression and 5-ASA efficacy, indicating that the intestinal clock coordinates the time-dependent response to 5-ASA. CONCLUSION: These findings identify FTH1 as a circadian-responsive factor linked to the time-dependent efficacy of 5-ASA and support circadian-guided optimization of 5-ASA administration as a potential strategy for improving UC treatment.

papers.abstract_en: AIM: The insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) and its downstream signaling pathways drive proliferation, survival, and extracellular matrix production, representing key therapeutic targets in thyroid eye disease (TED). This novel in vitro study investigated the inhibitory effects of the dual IGF-1R/insulin receptor small-molecule inhibitor Linsitinib on orbital target cell activity, proliferation, and survival. METHODS: Human orbital fibroblasts (OF) were pre-treated with increasing doses of Linsitinib and stimulated with 100 ng/mL IGF-1 to quantify hyaluronic acid (HA) and pro-collagen in supernatants via ELISA. Intracellular protein kinase B (AKT) phosphorylation at Serine 473 was quantified in cell lysates. Additionally, an equimolar comparison between Linsitinib and the anti-IGF-1R monoclonal antibody Teprotumumab was performed in IGF-1R-expressing cells. Proliferation was assessed both microscopically and by tetrazolium assay, while apoptosis was evaluated by caspase-3/7 activity. RESULTS: Linsitinib markedly suppressed IGF-1-induced HA and pro-collagen secretion, with TED OF showing significantly greater sensitivity and exclusive morphological evidence of apoptosis compared to control OF. Linsitinib effectively inhibited IGF-1-induced AKT phosphorylation to baseline levels in OF. Equimolar comparison in IGF-1R-expressing cells demonstrated that Linsitinib outperformed Teprotumumab in inhibiting cell proliferation across most tested concentrations, whereas Teprotumumab showed higher potency only at the lowest concentrations. While Teprotumumab failed to induce cell death, Linsitinib triggered robust activity of the apoptosis markers caspase-3/7. Morphologically, in contrast to Teprotumumab, Linsitinib induced dose-dependent changes characterized by cellular contraction and formation of gaps in the monolayer. CONCLUSION: Linsitinib reverses OF activation through intracellular kinase blockade while outperforming Teprotumumab in equimolar comparison. These findings highlight the role of Linsitinib as a potent, dual-targeted therapy for TED.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: There are three human apolipoprotein E (E) isoforms: E2, E3, and E4. Compared with E3, E4 is an AD risk factor. West Nile Virus (WNV) can cause neurological disease, and it results in some neuropathology and neuroinflammation seen in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Previously, we reported on the effects of exposure to the Kunjin strain (KUNV) of WNV in middle-aged knock-in (KI) mice expressing human amyloid precursor protein (APP) containing the dominant NL-G-F mutations with human apoE targeted replacement (TR) mice on behavioral, immune, and pathological measures, and circadian body temperatures. NL-G-F/E4 mice were more susceptible to KUNV-induced cognitive injury and prolonged viral load in the cortex; viral load was detected in the cortex of more mice expressing amyloid precursor protein with the dominant NL-G-F AD mutations and expressing also E4 than those expressing also E3. As NL-G-F and NL-G-F/apoE mice show cognitive injury and neuropathology at 6 months of age and age is a risk factor to develop AD and modulates the immune response in AD, we assessed in this study whether genotype differences in response to KUNV exposure are seen in younger mice. To determine whether the presence of NL-G-F is required to detect genotype differences in response to KUNV and/or modulates the response to KUNV, E3 and E4 mice were included as well. As compared with E3, E2 reduces the risk to develop AD and the vast majority of AD would likely not occur in the absence of E3 and E4 NL-G-F/E2 mice were included in this study as well. METHODS: We crossed knock-in (KI) mice expressing human amyloid precursor protein (APP) containing the dominant NL-G-F mutations with human apoE targeted replacement (TR) mice and used middle-aged NL-G-F/E3 and NL-G-F/E4 mice to assess the role of WNV (subtype Kunjin virus) (KUNV) exposure on behavioral alteration performance, circadian body temperatures, viral loads, neuropathology, and transcript levels of three immune measures in cortex important in the detrimental effects of KUNV on brain function. RESULTS: There were apoE isoform-dependent responses to KUNV exposure on various measures already seen at 6 months of age and are mostly more profound in the absence than in the presence of NL-G-F. One week following exposure, cortical insoluble p-tau levels were lower in KUNV- than PBS-treated apoE, but not NL-G-F/apoE mice. Soluble p-tau levels in cortex were higher in KUNV- than PBS-treated mice, and this effect was more pronounced in NL-G-F/apoE than apoE mice. The insoluble/soluble p-tau ratio was lower in KUNV- than PBS-treated mice, and this effect was more pronounced in apoE than NL-G-F/apoE. DISCUSSION: These results are consistent with results in cultured cells supporting that Aβ and p-tau might have antiviral properties.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The escalating global incidence of multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae necessitates an effective vaccine. While the meningococcal 4CMenB vaccine offers some cross-protection against gonorrhoea, this protection is limited highlighting the need for a targeted gonococcal vaccine. In this study, we evaluate the durability of immune response and characterise the immunogenicity induced by GonoVac, a native Outer Membrane Vesicle (nOMV) vaccine produced from N. gonorrhoeae GC_0817560lpxL1- , across genetically distinct strains of mouse. METHODS: We evaluated the longevity of the immune response induced by two and three doses of GonoVac formulated with aluminium hydroxide (Al(OH)3) over a one-year period (49 weeks for C57BL/6 and CD1 mice, 33 weeks for BALB/c mice), compared to the meningococcal group B vaccine, 4CMenB. Identical immunisation schedules were followed in BALB/c, C57BL/6, and CD1 mice. Separately, we examined the impact of Al(OH)3 on GonoVac immunogenicity in all three mouse strains. Serological, mucosal, and cellular responses were assessed using ELISA, serum bactericidal assays (SBA) and ELISpot. RESULTS: GonoVac with Al(OH)3 induced robust, long-lasting anti-gonococcal IgG responses in all three strains of mice and significantly higher levels of antibody-dependent complement-mediated killing of gonococci in C57BL/6 and CD1 mice compared with 4CMenB. Immune responses were maintained for up to one year. Serum anti-gonococcal IgG subclass distributions varied across mouse strains and between GonoVac and 4CMenB in the same strain of mouse. GonoVac formulated with and without Al(OH)3 elicited high levels of antibody-dependent complement-mediated killing of N. gonorrhoeae irrespective of mouse strain. While mucosal IgG responses were robust with both GonoVac formulations, Al(OH)3 significantly enhancing cellular immunity in BALB/c and CD1 mice compared with C57BL/6 mice. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that GonoVac, a preclinical candidate gonococcal nOMV vaccine, induces durable and functional anti-gonococcal immune responses that are higher than 4CMenB, across three commonly used laboratory strains of mice.
