papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Combination chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of breast cancer (BC) treatment, yet the relative contribution of individual drugs within standard regimens remains poorly understood. We investigated whether the activity of the widely used anthracycline-cyclophosphamide-taxane (AC-T) regimen reflects uniform benefit from all constituent drugs or heterogeneous drug-specific vulnerabilities across tumors. Methods: We combined in silico drug-response analyses, functional validation in BC cell lines, and ex vivo profiling in patient-derived organoids (PDOs). Drug responses were integrated into the Probability of Chemotherapeutic Efficacy (PCE), a multidimensional response metric combining relative drug potency, maximal efficacy, and clinically achievable free-drug exposure. To explore the broader applicability of PCE, we additionally applied it to an independent publicly available GR-based pharmacological dataset generated by the HMS LINCS Center. Results: Across BC models, anthracyclines and taxanes displayed only partially overlapping sensitivity profiles, indicating distinct drug-specific vulnerabilities. Functional validation in 2D cell lines and PDOs confirmed highly context-dependent responses to AC-T components. Among 21 PDOs with complete drug-response datasets, extensive interpatient heterogeneity was observed, with non-overlapping patterns of sensitivity to A, C, and T. Responses were better represented as a continuum of functional vulnerability states than as binary sensitive-versus-resistant categories. AC generated the highest proportion of favorable response profiles, with 62% of PDOs classified as partial response-like or complete response-like, compared with 48% for A, 38% for C, and 14% for T. AC activity was positively associated with the most active constituent drug within each PDO. Application of this framework to an independent public dataset produced biologically plausible response patterns consistent with the molecular characteristics of the evaluated breast cancer cell lines, supporting its computational transferability. Conclusions: These findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in the contribution of individual drugs to AC-T activity and are compatible with a model in which different tumors derive benefit from different regimen components. Together, these findings establish a hypothesis-generating functional framework for dissecting the contribution of individual drugs within combination chemotherapy regimens. Prospective studies correlating PDO-derived functional responses with clinical outcomes will be required to determine the predictive value and potential clinical utility of this approach before informing therapeutic decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: Background: This retrospective study introduces imaging inner tumor margin patterns (iITMP) and evaluates their correlation with pathological Worst pattern of invasion (WPOI) in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (OTSCC). Associations of iITMP with pathological primary tumor category (pT), histologic grade, perineural invasion (PNI), nodal metastasis, and extranodal extension (ENE) were assessed. Correlations between imaging depth of invasion (iDOI) and pathological DOI (pDOI), and between imaging primary tumor (iT) and pT, PNI, and ENE were evaluated. Methods: Baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) from January 2021 to December 2022 of 224 upfront-operated OTSCC patients was reviewed by two blinded radiologists using contrast-enhanced thin-slice. iITMP (types 1-3) were classified based on inner tumor margin morphology. iDOI was measured after excluding peritumoral hyperenhancement. Correlation between categorical and continuous variables were assessed using Kappa statistics and Spearman's test respectively. Associations between categorical variables were analyzed using Fisher's exact or Pearson's chi-squared tests. Univariable and multivariable analyses were additionally performed. Results: The mean patient age was 47 ± 11 years. Substantial agreement was observed between iITMP and WPOI, and between iT and pT. iDOI strongly correlated with pDOI. iITMP was significantly associated with pT, irregular (iITMP2) and infiltrative (iITMP3) margins were associated with PNI only on univariate analysis, while iITMP was not an independent predictor on multivariable analysis. iT significantly correlated with PNI and ENE. Conclusions: iITMP strongly correlate with WPOI and is substantially associated with pT categories. iT categories show significant association with PNI and ENE. Therefore, iITMP and iT may serve as potential imaging biomarkers of adverse histopathological features in OTSCC.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Oral leukoplakia (OL) is a common oral potentially malignant disorder, but prediction of malignant progression remains challenging. This study investigated miR-21-5p and miR-21-3p expression in healthy oral mucosa, OL with epithelial dysplasia, and early oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), together with clinicopathological associations. Methods: Sixty participants were divided into three groups: exposure-free healthy controls (n = 20), histopathologically confirmed OL with epithelial dysplasia (n = 20), and early OSCC (pT1-2N0M0; n = 20). Expression was quantified by RT-qPCR and evaluated using exploratory correlation, regression, Welch's ANOVA, and Games-Howell comparisons. Results: miR-21-5p differed significantly among groups (p < 0.001). Expression was lower in OL than in healthy controls and early OSCC (both p < 0.001), whereas early OSCC and controls did not differ (p = 0.997). miR-21-5p was inversely associated with dysplasia grade (Spearman's ρ = -0.54, p = 0.013; unstandardized regression coefficient B = -0.646, p = 0.017). miR-21-3p was numerically higher in early OSCC, but its overall group difference was not significant (p = 0.051). Conclusions: The two mature miR-21 strands showed distinct, non-linear expression patterns across the three groups. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating; the cross-sectional design does not establish predictive or prognostic value, and validation in larger longitudinal cohorts is required. The unexpected miR-21-5p pattern remains unexplained and requires independent validation.

papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common liver cancer and usually develops on a background of cirrhotic liver. Early and accurate diagnosis enables potentially curative interventions. HCC surveillance, usually offered to patients at risk for HCC, such as those with cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B infection, and previous diagnosis of HCC, is associated with earlier detection and improved survival. In these patients, the diagnosis can be established non-invasively without histological confirmation when the imaging-based LI-RADS criteria are met. Tissue biopsy is mandatory for establishing diagnosis in patients without cirrhosis or other risk factors for HCC, differentiating HCC from other malignant and non-malignant entities, especially when imaging features are not conclusive. In this review, we discuss the evolving role of tissue biopsy beyond establishing the diagnosis, in providing important prognostic information and enabling precise histopathological classification. Features such as poor differentiation, microvascular invasion, and a pattern of vessels encapsulating tumor clusters are linked to worse prognosis. HCC is characterized by heterogeneity, with different histological subtypes associated with distinct clinical and radiological features and distinct biology. Emerging data from molecular profiling and immune-microenvironment studies enable further classification into proliferative versus non-proliferative molecular subgroups and inflamed versus non-inflamed immune subtypes. This more refined characterization of HCC carries important implications not only for prognostication but also for predicting response to immunotherapy. In the future, the combination of imaging features that correlate with molecular signatures, novel serum biomarkers, and liquid biopsy may provide less invasive tools for early detection, risk stratification, and guide personalized therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Retroperitoneal sarcomas (RPS) are rare malignancies that pose challenges due to their large size and proximity to organs-at-risk (OARs). Compared to conventional 5-week radiation therapy (RT), hypofractionated RT (HFRT) offers a shorter alternative with potential biologic benefit, and simultaneous integrated boost (SIB) can increase delivered dose. We evaluated the dosimetric feasibility of HFRT with a central tumor SIB for bulky RPS. Methods: Fifteen patients with RPS previously treated with preoperative conventionally fractionated RT were replanned using HFRT with a central SIB. Volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) plans were created to deliver 42.75 Gy in 15 fractions to the planning target volume (PTV), 45 Gy to the internal gross tumor volume (iGTV), and 52.5 Gy to the SIB volume (1 cm contraction of iGTV). OAR planning objectives were prioritized during optimization. Dosimetric plan-generation feasibility was defined as generation of a treatment plan meeting prespecified target-coverage criteria; compliance with each OAR objective was assessed separately. Results: Mean tumor size was 18.3 cm (range 5.8-28.2 cm), with mean volumes for iGTV, SIB, and PTV of 1633.8 cc, 926.9 cc, and 3323.2 cc, respectively. All plans met the prespecified target coverage criteria for iGTV, SIB, and PTV. Ten of 15 plans met all target-coverage criteria and all prespecified OAR objectives; five met the target coverage criteria and non-bowel OAR objectives but exceeded at least one bowel objective by <1% of the specified constraint. All non-bowel OAR objectives were met except that the bilateral kidney objective was exceeded in 4 of 11 evaluable patients. The average homogeneity index for the iGTV and SIB were 0.21 (range 0.18-0.25) and 0.05 (range 0.04-0.06), respectively. The PTV 95% conformality index was 0.99 (range 0.97-1.0), indicating excellent target conformation with minimal normal tissue spillage. Conclusions: These findings support the dosimetric feasibility of generating hypofractionated radiation therapy plans with a central SIB for large retroperitoneal sarcomas. However, one-third of plans exceeded at least one bowel objective, and these planning results do not establish clinical deliverability, safety, or efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Recurrent oral squamous cell carcinoma (rOSCC) is associated with a poor prognosis, and evidence supporting risk stratification in the salvage setting remains limited. The prognostic value of conventional staging systems and tumor-related characteristics after recurrence has not yet been fully established. METHODS: We conducted a single-center observational study including patients with rOSCC who had previously undergone treatment for pT1-2 N0M0 OSCC, all subsequently surgically salvaged. Clinical, histopathological, and recurrence-related variables were collected. Recurrent tumors were classified according to the AJCC TNM staging system, the Composite Oral Cavity and Oropharynx Recurrence Staging System (CORSS), and the Same-Up-Down staging system (SUDss), a novel staging system developed by our group. RESULTS: A total of 49 patients were included. Several pathological characteristics, including the rT3-4 category (p = 0.025), perineural invasion (p < 0.001), lymphovascular invasion (p = 0.003), greater depth of invasion (p = 0.011), nodal involvement (p = 0.002), and higher rTNM (p = 0.004) and CORSS stage (stage II p = 0.012; stage III p = 0.038) were associated with poorer OS in univariable analyses. In multivariable analysis, CORSS stage II (HR 2.89, 95% CI 1.04-8.04; p = 0.041) and stage III (HR 12.73, 95% CI 2.11-76.68; p = 0.005), as well as close/positive surgical margins (HR 2.57, 95% CI 0.99-6.71; p = 0.045) and pathological nodal involvement (HR 4.82, 95% CI 1.77-13.14; p = 0.002), were independently associated with poorer OS. CONCLUSIONS: CORSS appears to offer complementary prognostic value compared with conventional rTNM in patients with surgically treated rOSCC, although formal comparative validation of discrimination and calibration is warranted. Pathological lymph node involvement and close or positive surgical margins were the most relevant independent adverse prognostic factors. These findings identify higher-risk patients but do not, by themselves, establish a benefit from treatment intensification.

papers.title_en: Next-generation natural killer cell therapy: bench to bedside and beyond.
papers.authors: Zhao A, Xu J, Deng W, Zhang M, Shao Y, Liu Y, Liang A, Wang X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Hematology, The Second Affiliated Hospital, College of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: NK细胞治疗已从基础发现发展为临床验证平台；CAR-NK在B细胞恶性肿瘤中显示显著疗效与更优安全性，并扩展至自身免疫病；实体瘤仍受抗原异质性、物理屏障和代谢敌对环境限制，需系统级工程重编程和临床转化参数优化。
papers.ai_note: 本文为叙述性综述，无原始研究设计、样本量、效应量或统计检验；摘要以“remarkable efficacy”等定性表述强调CAR-NK在血液肿瘤和自身免疫病的获益，但未给出主要终点数值或证据等级；对实体瘤挑战有提及。信息不足：无法评估偏倚风险、疗效幅度及胸外科适用性。
papers.reason: 为NK/CAR-NK免疫治疗在血液肿瘤、自身免疫病及实体瘤中的转化现状提供框架性综述，可用于科研选题和免疫治疗背景梳理，但对胸外科手术决策直接影响有限。
papers.abstract_en: Natural killer (NK) cells have emerged as central players in cancer immunotherapy, progressing from basic discovery to clinically validated platforms over five decades. This review synthesizes the evolving understanding of NK cell biology, including subset heterogeneity, epigenetic regulation, and metabolic control, and, as innovative focal points, intratumoral NK heterogeneity, epigenetic modulation, and intracellular immune checkpoints, forming the foundation for rational therapeutic engineering. We examine the clinical trajectory from unmodified adoptive transfer to cytokine-induced memory-like NK cells and, most transformatively, to chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-NK cells. Landmark trials have established the remarkable efficacy and superior safety of CAR-NK cells in B-cell malignancies, with recent studies extending these benefits to autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis, demonstrating durable immune reset with a favorable safety profile. Despite these advances, solid tumors remain formidable challenges, hindered by antigen heterogeneity, physical barriers, and a metabolically hostile microenvironment. We therefore analyze next-generation engineering strategies that move beyond single modifications toward systems-level reprogramming, encompassing intrinsic enhancements (cytokine signaling, metabolic fitness, checkpoint disruption), extrinsic tumor microenvironment remodeling, and advanced delivery platforms. We further synthesize the practical dimensions of clinical translation by systematically examining key optimization parameters that will guide the path toward precision NK cell therapy. These include rational dosing and scheduling regimens, strategies to reduce lymphodepletion intensity, context-dependent persistence requirements across different disease indications and the emerging biomarker landscape.

papers.abstract_en: Lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) contributes substantially to primary graft dysfunction after lung transplantation and also occurs in other clinical settings involving transient interruption and restoration of pulmonary blood flow. O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification is rapidly altered by cellular stress, yet its role in acute pulmonary ischemia-reperfusion remains incompletely understood. We investigated this question using a murine model of transient left pulmonary hilar occlusion followed by reperfusion and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in MLE-12 cells. O-GlcNAcylation was increased pharmacologically with the O-GlcNAcase inhibitor Thiamet G and reduced with the O-GlcNAc transferase inhibitor OSMI-4. Global O-GlcNAc levels, indices of tissue and cellular injury, and Caspase-1/GSDMD-related pyroptotic signaling were then examined. In both models, O-GlcNAcylation increased early after ischemic stress, whereas pyroptosis-related changes became more pronounced as injury progressed. Thiamet G preserved MLE-12 cell viability, reduced LDH release, and lessened histopathological damage, pulmonary edema, and alveolar-capillary protein leakage in vivo. These effects were accompanied by lower Caspase-1 activation, reduced GSDMD cleavage, and fewer Caspase-1/PI double-positive cells. OSMI-4 produced the opposite pattern, with greater tissue and cellular injury and stronger pyroptosis-related signaling. The protective effect of Thiamet G was also weakened when OSMI-4 was given concurrently. These findings indicate that the early rise in O-GlcNAcylation is consistent with an acute stress response to LIRI. Pharmacologically maintaining higher O-GlcNAcylation was associated with less severe injury and weaker Caspase-1/GSDMD-related signaling, supporting further investigation of this modification as a therapeutic target in acute LIRI.

papers.results: 检测器外部泛化：队列宏观AUROC 0.816；裁决子集0.879。层面筛选非劣但无获益（几乎所有高置信检出已位于锚定器官轴位范围内）；器官状态融合仅胆囊炎AUROC改善（假设生成性）。单次运行中，加入器官图训练使内部测试mAP@0.5由0.482升至0.517，模型依赖该图谱，但外部宏观AUROC未改善（0.822 vs 0.829；Δ -0.007，95% CI -0.019至+0.007），肾结石AUROC下降（0.678 vs 0.768；探索性），与使用他人图谱时不同。按站点重校准为最有效的操作点调整（宏观F1 +0.021）；无标注微调降低判别力。
papers.authors_conclusion: 显式解剖信息，无论应用于检测之后还是训练之中，均未改善该检测器的整体外部判别力；按站点重校准带来最大的操作点增益。
papers.ai_note: 主要终点（外部AUROC）为阴性，但摘要以内部测试mAP@0.5提升（0.517 vs 0.482）与胆囊炎亚组AUROC改善（未给数值，自标为假设生成性）作为亮点呈现，存在选择性强调倾向；训练实验为“单次运行”，缺乏随机种子重复，0.517 vs 0.482的内部差异稳定性信息不足；肾结石AUROC下降被标为探索性，与“使用他人图谱”的对照结果仅定性描述，未给数值；主要终点（各Arm A/B/C对比单独检测器）的AUROC差值与置信区间未在摘要中报告，信息不足；外部标签来源于语言模型报告，参考标准仅覆盖280例嵌套子集，标签噪声对阴性结论的影响未量化。

pico.p: 827例外院Stanford Merlin CT检查（语言模型报告标签），其中280例经放射科医师裁决的嵌套子集为参考标准
pico.ic: 干预：基于通用器官分割模型（TotalSegmentator）的解剖先验——TS衍生层面筛选（Arm A）、器官状态融合（Arm B）、二者联合（Arm C），以及在训练中加入患者本人或他人TS器官图作为额外输入通道；对照：单独检测器（YOLOv11），在冻结、重校准与微调条件下比较；AUROC为主要终点，采用配对研究级bootstrap

papers.reason: 为“在成熟影像检测器上叠加通用解剖先验是否值得”这一AI开发决策提供了严谨的阴性外部验证证据，并指出按站点重校准比解剖先验更能改善操作点，可直接影响院内AI部署与后处理流程选择；同时为同类外部验证队列设计提供对照基线。
papers.abstract_en: To test whether anatomical priors from a general-purpose organ segmentation model (TotalSegmentator, TS), applied at inference or during training, improve an externally validated YOLOv11 detector for six acute abdominal emergencies. The frozen detector was applied to 827 external Stanford Merlin CT studies with language-model report labels; a nested 280-study radiologist-adjudicated subset was the reference standard. TS-derived slice selection (Arm A), organ-state integration (Arm B), and their combination (Arm C) were compared with the detector alone under frozen, recalibrated, and fine-tuned conditions. The detector was also retrained from scratch (identical 10-epoch budget) with image channels only, with the patient's TS organ maps as added input channels, or with another patient's maps. AUROC was primary; comparisons used a paired study-level bootstrap. The detector generalized externally (macro AUROC 0.816 cohort; 0.879 adjudicated). Slice selection was non-inferior but not beneficial: nearly all confident detections already lay within the anchored organ's axial range; organ-state fusion improved AUROC only for cholecystitis (hypothesis-generating). In single runs, training with organ maps raised internal test mAP@0.5 (0.517 versus 0.482), and the model depended on the maps, but external macro AUROC did not improve (0.822 versus 0.829; Δ -0.007, 95% CI -0.019 to +0.007) and kidney-stone AUROC fell (0.678 versus 0.768; exploratory), unlike with another patient's maps. Per-site recalibration was the most effective operating-point adjustment (macro F1 +0.021); annotation-free fine-tuning reduced discrimination. Explicit anatomy, applied after detection or during training, did not improve this detector's overall external discrimination. Per-site recalibration gave the largest operating-point gain.

papers.title_zh: ARPI经治后mCRPC的后续治疗序贯：尚无前瞻性序贯试验，基于II/III期证据的叙述性综述与假设性四轨框架
papers.title_en: Treatment Sequencing in ARPI-Pre-Exposed Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Radioligand Therapy, PARP Inhibitors, and Antibody-Drug Conjugates.
papers.authors: Sharaf B, Al-Rwashdeh M, El Khatib O, Al-Ibraheem A, Abu Fara A, Ismail A, Alkasrawi H, Abdalla M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Internal Medicine, King Hussein Cancer Center (KHCC), Amman 11941, Jordan.
papers.results: 无前瞻性序贯试验报告。CARD：卡巴他赛 vs 多西他赛后ARPI转换，OS HR 0.64。PROfound cohort A：OS HR 0.69；TALAPRO-2 全人群：OS HR 0.80；TRITON3 中 BRCA 的 OS 未改善（HR 0.91）。PSMAfore：177Lu-PSMA-617 较 ARPI 转换改善 rPFS，但意向性治疗 OS 无差异（HR 0.91），交叉率60%。无含紫杉类对照的试验显示 OS 优势；PLUDO 初步数据显示 OS 倾向先用多西他赛（HR 1.64）。
papers.authors_conclusion: 提出一个以同源重组修复状态和PSMA-PET表达分层的、产生假设的四轨框架；治疗选择仍应个体化。
papers.ai_note: 本文为叙述性综述，检索与筛选流程、去重及偏倚评估未在摘要中描述，证据分级由作者自定，存在选择性纳入可能；PLUDO 为初步数据且作者自认受非对称交叉混杂，其 HR 1.64 不宜作为序贯结论；PSMAfore 的 rPFS 阳性与 ITT OS 阴性（60%交叉）被并列陈述，需注意以 rPFS 替代 OS 解读的风险；TRITON3 的 BRCA OS 阴性结果与 PROfound/TALAPRO-2 的阳性结果人群定义不同（cohort A、全人群 vs BRCA），跨试验 HR 不可直接比较；四轨框架为专家意见性假设，无验证数据。

pico.p: ARPI强化治疗后进展的转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）人群（综述，未合并样本量）
pico.ic: 后续治疗策略比较：卡巴他赛 vs ARPI转换、PARP抑制剂（按HRR状态）、177Lu-PSMA-617 vs ARPI转换、多西他赛序贯先后（无前瞻性随机序贯试验）

papers.reason: 为ARPI经治后mCRPC的后续治疗选择提供证据边界：明确目前不存在前瞻性序贯试验，卡巴他赛仍是最清晰对照数据，PARP抑制剂与177Lu-PSMA-617的OS获益受交叉与人群限定影响，可作为设计序贯随机试验与解读单臂数据的参照基线。
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) intensification in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer has changed the population reaching metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), and the optimal sequence of subsequent therapies is uncertain. Methods: The study presents a narrative review of phase II/III trials reporting radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) or overall survival (OS) in mCRPC, including congress data, to June 2026, graded on a five-level evidence hierarchy. Results: No prospective sequencing trial has been reported. CARD (cabazitaxel versus an ARPI switch after docetaxel; OS HR 0.64) remains the clearest sequencing dataset. Alpha-controlled OS benefit for PARP inhibitors is established in the PROfound cohort A (HR 0.69) and in the TALAPRO-2 all-comer population (HR 0.80); larger BRCA-specific estimates are exploratory, and BRCA OS in TRITON3 was not improved (HR 0.91). 177Lu-PSMA-617 improved rPFS versus an ARPI switch in PSMAfore, but intention-to-treat OS did not differ (HR 0.91) amid 60% crossover; no taxane-controlled trial has shown an OS advantage, and in preliminary PLUDO data, OS favoured docetaxel first (HR 1.64), a difference potentially confounded by asymmetric crossover. Conclusions: We propose a hypothesis-generating four-track framework stratified by homologous recombination repair status and PSMA-PET expression; treatment choice remains individualised.

papers.abstract_en: Pain is one of the most frequent and burdensome symptoms of pancreatic cancer and may substantially impair quality of life throughout the disease trajectory. Its complex and evolving etiology, involving visceral, neuropathic, somatic, and treatment-related mechanisms, frequently makes adequate pain control challenging. This critical narrative review provides a multidisciplinary overview of pancreatic cancer-associated pain management, integrating oncological treatment, palliative and pharmacological care, and interventional pain management into a practical clinical framework. Anticancer therapies, including chemotherapy and radiotherapy, may provide clinically meaningful analgesia in addition to their disease-controlling effect. Early integration of palliative care enables repeated symptom assessment, individualized pharmacological treatment, and management of the psychological, social, and spiritual dimensions of total pain. When conventional analgesic strategies provide insufficient relief or cause intolerable adverse effects, interventional techniques such as coeliac plexus neurolysis, splanchnic neurolysis, or intrathecal drug delivery can complement ongoing oncological and palliative treatment. Rather than following a rigid stepwise analgesic approach, pancreatic cancer-associated pain management should be individualized according to pain mechanism, disease stage and anatomy, previous treatments, functional status, expected survival, and patient preferences. Based on the available evidence and multidisciplinary clinical considerations, we propose a practical patient-centered pathway that dynamically integrates disease-directed, pharmacological, supportive, and interventional strategies throughout the disease course. Early multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous reassessment may facilitate timely treatment escalation and improve pain control while minimizing treatment burden.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs) remain a major determinant of long-term outcome. Although hepatic resection offers the best chance of durable survival, the definition of resectability has evolved beyond technical feasibility alone. This review aims to provide a structured overview of contemporary management strategies for patients with upfront technically resectable or synchronous CRLM, with emphasis on patient selection, tumor biology, perioperative systemic therapy, margin strategy, and surgical sequencing. Methods: A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was performed to identify studies published between 2000 and 2026. Eligible studies evaluated surgical, liver-directed, or systemic treatment strategies for CRLMs and reported outcomes including overall survival, disease-free survival, recurrence, margin status, or perioperative morbidity. Given the heterogeneity of the available evidence, findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Contemporary management of CRLMs requires integration of patient fitness, technical resectability, and tumor biology. In upfront technically resectable disease, routine neoadjuvant chemotherapy has not consistently improved overall survival, whereas selected high-risk patients may benefit from short-course preoperative therapy. Margin strategy is increasingly biology-informed rather than based on a universal margin width. In synchronous disease, no single operative sequence is superior for all patients; treatment should be selected according to disease burden, operative complexity, and the need to preserve access to systemic therapy. Conclusions: Management of upfront resectable and synchronous CRLMs should be individualized through multidisciplinary assessment. Current evidence supports a risk-adapted strategy that integrates technical feasibility, patient factors, and tumor biology while recognizing persistent uncertainty regarding optimal chemotherapy timing and surgical sequencing.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To map and synthesise the existing evidence on people's perspectives and requirements for patient-facing digital health technologies for use in prostate cancer care delivery. Understanding the preferences of people with prostate cancer and understanding the barriers and facilitators to maximising engagement with digital supportive care healthcare landscape. METHODS: Four electronic databases were searched to identify suitable studies. All identified citations were imported into Covidence systematic review software for the removal of duplicate records and the study selection process by two reviewers. Methodological quality was appraised using the MMAT, and findings were synthesised narratively using the Human, Organisation, and Technology-fit (HOT-fit) evaluation framework. RESULTS: Eighty-eight studies were included and represented a total of 29,256 participants affected by prostate cancer. Preferences for digital supportive care emerged across four interconnected domains: (1) mode of delivery, (2) type of content desired, (3) factors enabling engagement, and (4) barriers limiting use. Overall, there was willingness to engage with digital models due to their convenience, flexibility, and immediacy of access. Self-management was enhanced via decision aids, symptom management tools, informational resources, and evidence-based tools to support aspects of psychosocial functioning and emotional wellbeing, physical activity, and sexual health. Several barriers to the implementation and uptake of digital supportive care interventions were identified primarily relating to technology access, device compatibility, digital literacy, and emotional readiness. CONCLUSIONS: Digital models in prostate cancer care were acceptable and valued for their convenience, flexibility, immediacy of access, tailored content, clinician support, and interactive features, and facilitated self-management through decision-making, symptom management, and informational and psychosocial support. Interpreted through the HOT-fit framework, their value depended on the fit between the technology, its users, and the care setting rather than on technological sophistication alone. Limited attention has been given to digital sexual wellbeing support, and further research is needed on engagement among people with low digital literacy, non-English speakers, and lower-income populations, and on the long-term sustainability of digital models.

papers.abstract_en: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a complex autoimmune disease marked by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. The high disease burden and impact on quality of life highlight the need for therapies that target underlying pathogenic mechanisms rather than merely treating organ-specific symptoms. Phosphodiesterases, including phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B), are key regulators of cellular function and inflammatory responses of several cell types central to SSc pathogenesis. Given PDE4B's broad effects, targeting it may provide benefits beyond organ-specific manifestations and improve current care. Selective PDE4B inhibition represents a novel therapeutic approach for SSc, with improved subtype selectivity compared with earlier pan-PDE4 inhibitors. Nerandomilast preferentially inhibits PDE4B (ninefold over PDE4D), potentially improving tolerability versus oral pan-PDE4 inhibitors by avoiding adverse events such as gastrointestinal intolerance. Preclinical findings in SSc-relevant mouse and cell models show that PDE4B inhibition modulates inflammatory cytokine secretion, smooth muscle cell tension, endothelial and epithelial barrier integrity, and extracellular matrix synthesis under oxidative stress; this suggests nerandomilast could attenuate immune dysregulation, fibrosis, and potentially impact vasculopathy. Two pivotal Phase III trials evaluated nerandomilast in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (FIBRONEER™-IPF; NCT05321069) and progressive pulmonary fibrosis (FIBRONEER™-ILD; NCT05321082), the latter of which included patients with SSc-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD). The ongoing CONQUEST trial (NCT06195072) is investigating the efficacy and safety of various drugs, including nerandomilast, in patients with early active SSc-ILD. This perspective highlights the rationale for targeting PDE4B in SSc therapy and explores preclinical findings in SSc and clinical findings in SSc-ILD to date.

papers.title_zh: G1浸润性乳腺癌中组织学亚型未提供显著额外预后信息：单中心回顾性队列（364例，亚型间总生存无显著差异）
papers.title_en: Histological Subtype Provides Limited Prognostic Information in Grade 1 Invasive Breast Carcinoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Locher E, Benning L, Varga Z
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pathology and Molecular Pathology, University Hospital Zurich, 8091 Zurich, Switzerland.
papers.results: NST占67.3%，纯特殊亚型15.1%，混合亚型15.7%；总体5年生存率94.7%，10年生存率85.4%；NST、纯特殊亚型与混合亚型间总生存无显著差异（log-rank p = 0.39）；各纯特殊亚型间亦无显著生存差异（p = 0.20）；组织学亚型与死亡无显著关联（χ2 p = 0.064）
papers.authors_conclusion: 在该G1浸润性乳腺癌队列中，未发现组织学亚型与总生存之间存在统计学显著关联；但鉴于队列异质性和事件数少，不能排除具有临床意义的差异，需更大样本、纳入多变量分析及乳腺癌特异性结局的研究进一步明确组织学亚型在G1浸润性乳腺癌中的预后价值。
papers.ai_note: 摘要仅报告log-rank与卡方检验的p值，未给出HR/RR及95%CI，也未进行多变量校正，无法判断混杂（如年龄、合并症、治疗）对结论的影响；生存分析队列由364例缩减至348例（排除对侧高级别癌），人群定义中途变动且未说明其余基线特征；纯特殊亚型内部比较的样本量极小、事件数少，p=0.20不具备排除差异的效能；死亡为全因死亡而非乳腺癌特异生存，可能稀释亚型效应；分组比例（67.3%/15.1%/15.7%）与“混合亚型最低生存但无差异”的表述之间未提供分层生存数值，存在仅以统计学阴性作结论、对临床相关差异未量化的风险。

pico.p: 2005-2014年单中心诊断为G1浸润性乳腺癌患者，初筛429例，符合纳入标准364例；排除同期对侧高级别癌后348例进入生存分析
pico.ic: 暴露/分组为组织学亚型：无特殊类型（NST）vs 纯特殊亚型 vs 混合亚型（另比较各纯特殊亚型）；无干预，参照组为NST

papers.reason: 为“G1乳腺癌是否需按组织学亚型进一步分层随访/辅助治疗决策”这一低级别乳腺癌管理问题提供了阴性对照基线，并提示单中心小事件数回顾性设计不足以支持亚型驱动的预后分层；对胸部肿瘤领域的直接参考价值有限，但可作为同类“亚型预后价值”回顾性队列的方法学与解读参照。
papers.abstract_en: Background: Histological grade is one of the strongest prognostic factors in invasive breast cancer. However, it remains unclear whether histological subtype provides additional prognostic information in well-differentiated (grade 1; G1) invasive breast carcinomas. This study investigated the distribution of histological subtypes in G1 breast cancers and evaluated their impact on overall survival. Methods: In this retrospective single-centre study, all patients diagnosed with G1 invasive breast carcinoma in a single institution between 2005 and 2014 were identified. Histopathological and clinical data were retrieved from institutional pathology and clinical databases. Tumours were classified as no special type (NST), pure special type, or mixed subtype. Overall survival was analysed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and compared with the log-rank test. Associations between histological subtype and mortality were evaluated using the chi-squared test. Results: Of 429 initially identified patients, 364 fulfilled the inclusion criteria. NST represented the predominant subtype (67.3%), whereas pure special types and mixed subtypes accounted for 15.1% and 15.7% of cases, respectively. Tubular carcinoma was the most frequent pure special subtype, followed by mucinous, cribriform, papillary, lobular and adenoid cystic carcinoma. After exclusion of patients with simultaneous higher-grade contralateral carcinomas, 348 patients were included in survival analyses. The overall 5- and 10-year survival rates were 94.7% and 85.4%, respectively. Pure special types showed the highest survival rates numerically, whereas mixed subtypes had the lowest. However, overall survival did not differ significantly between NST, pure special types and mixed subtypes (log-rank p = 0.39). Likewise, no significant survival differences were observed among individual pure special subtypes (p = 0.20), and no significant association between histological subtype and mortality was identified (χ2p = 0.064). Conclusions: Within this cohort of G1 invasive breast carcinomas, no statistically significant association between histological subtype and overall survival was identified. However, clinically relevant differences cannot be excluded given the heterogeneity of the cohort and the small number of events. Larger studies incorporating multivariable analyses and breast cancer-specific outcomes are needed to further clarify the prognostic relevance of histological subtype in G1 invasive breast cancer.

papers.abstract_en: CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) in the upper respiratory tract (URT) limit viral replication after transmission and prevent spread to the lower respiratory tract (LRT), whereas LRT CD8+ TRM are important for limiting immunopathology in the lung and promoting efficient viral clearance. Although the presence of local respiratory antigen is thought to be required for CD8+ TRM development in the LRT but not the URT, the relationship between local antigen encounter and cytokine signaling that influences TRM differentiation in distinct niches of the respiratory tract remains unknown. Here, we show using murine models that while URT TRM generated in the presence or absence of local respiratory antigen are phenotypically, transcriptionally, and functionally similar throughout the respiratory tract, their developmental pathways are compartmentally distinct and characterized by a context-dependent compensatory relationship between antigen and cytokine signaling. In the absence of local antigen, URT CD8+ TRM formation required TGF-β signaling, and notably, while both IL-15 and IL-33 were broadly dispensable in the URT, IL-33 was able to rescue LRT CD8+ TRM development in the absence of local antigen. Together, these findings highlight key differences for CD8+ TRM development in distinct areas of the respiratory tract, offering valuable insights into the development of mucosal cellular immunity following intranasal and parenteral vaccination.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has demonstrated limited efficacy in microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC). The fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling pathway contributes to tumor immune evasion, yet its role in CRC remains insufficiently understood. We investigated the immunomodulatory effects of FGFR inhibition in combination with PD-1 blockade in murine CRC models. In vitro co-culture systems were used to evaluate T cell activation upon FGFR3 blockade. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset evaluation, were conducted to elucidate molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance. Combined FGFR inhibition and PD-1 blockade significantly reduced T cell exhaustion and promoted macrophage repolarization toward an antitumor phenotype. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of immune-related pathways and activation of immune-stimulatory genes. In vitro, FGFR3-specific monoclonal antibody treatment enhanced IFNg release following PD-1 blockade. Moreover, analysis of TCGA data demonstrated that high FGFR3 expression correlates with worse prognosis in CRC patients. Our findings suggest that FGFR pathway inhibition may enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade and provide a rationale for further investigation of FGFR-targeted combination strategies in MSS CRC.

papers.title_zh: 伴抑郁症状的肺癌患者静息态功能连接改变：一项探索性横断面fMRI研究
papers.title_en: Altered resting-state functional connectivity in lung cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms.
papers.authors: Zhou H, Tang W, Ren H, Li K, Ren N, Li R, Duan J, Wang D et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Science and Mental Health, Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beiji…
papers.results: 伴抑郁症状组在8对脑区之间显示RS-FC改变：左侧距状皮层-右侧小脑IV-V小叶、左侧内侧额回-左侧前扣带回、左侧岛叶-左侧颞中回、左侧中央前回-左侧小脑III小叶、左侧丘脑-蚓部I和II、右侧嗅皮层-右侧梭状回、右侧直回-右侧小脑VIIb小叶、右侧小脑VIIb小叶-右侧嗅区。抑郁症状总分与多个脑区间的RS-FC呈负相关：左侧额上回与右侧颞中回 r=-0.72, p<0.001；左侧额上回与左侧颞极颞中回 r=-0.69, p<0.001；左侧三角部额下回与左侧颞极颞中回 r=-0.65, p<0.001；左侧内侧额上回与右侧颞中回 r=-0.65, p<0.001；左侧岛叶与右侧小脑脚II r=-0.6, p<0.001；右侧颞上回与右侧小脑脚II r=-0.67, p<0.001。
papers.authors_conclusion: 研究结果提示肺癌患者抑郁症状与RS-FC改变之间存在初步关联，且连接改变与症状严重程度相关；但由于未系统采集精神药物使用、癌症相关症状（如疼痛、疲乏）及治疗细节，这些发现应视为初步的、产生假设性的结果，而非共病抑郁的确定性标志物；未来需要系统评估药物、治疗及多维症状负担的纵向研究来确定这些连接模式是特异反映抑郁症状还是更广泛的癌症相关后遗效应。
papers.ai_note: 横断面设计无因果方向；作者自述未采集精神药物、疼痛/疲乏等症状与治疗细节，混杂无法排除（精神药物本身即强烈影响RS-FC）。组间8对脑区差异未报告任何统计量或校正方式；6项相关分析r达-0.6至-0.72，在33例样本中属异常高值，摘要未提及多重比较校正、PHQ-9切点或是否控制年龄/性别/治疗，存在选择性报告与P值膨胀风险。摘要为结论性表述，未给出效应量置信区间。

pico.p: 33例伴抑郁症状的肺癌患者与42例年龄、性别匹配的无抑郁症状肺癌患者（接受过异质性治疗的中国肺癌人群）
pico.ic: 干预/暴露：伴抑郁症状（PHQ-9评估）vs 不伴抑郁症状；对照指标：全脑静息态功能连接（RS-FC）

papers.reason: 为肺癌患者抑郁共病的神经影像标记提供初步对照基线，提示抑郁症状与功能连接的相关性，但尚不足以改变临床筛查或转诊决策，主要价值在于为后续纵向、控制药物与症状混杂的研究提供假设与设计参照。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: It is quite common clinically for cancer patients (including those with lung cancer) to have comorbid depressive symptoms. Numerous studies have shown that patients with depression often have altered resting-state functional connectivity (RS-FC). However, only a few studies have reported abnormal RS-FC in cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms. This exploratory and cross-sectional study examined a heterogeneously treated Chinese lung cancer population. Data on psychotropic medication, cancer-related symptoms, and detailed treatment histories were not systematically collected. The main objective was to observe the relationship between comorbid depressive symptoms and RS-FC in this population, which has not been reported yet. METHODS: We calculated whole-brain RS-FC in 33 lung cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms and 42 age- and sex-matched lung cancer patients without comorbid depressive symptoms. The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) was used to assess depressive symptoms in lung cancer patients. RESULTS: Compared to lung cancer patients without depressive symptoms, those with comorbid depressive symptoms showed altered RS-FC across eight brain region pairs: (1) left calcarine cortex-right cerebellar lobules IV-V, (2) left medial frontal gyrus-left anterior cingulate gyrus, (3) left insular-left middle temporal gyrus, (4) left precentral gyrus-left cerebellar lobule Ⅲ, (5) left thalamus-vermis Ⅰ and Ⅱ, (6) right olfactory cortex-right fusiform gyrus, (7) right rectus gyrus-right cerebellar lobule Ⅶ b, and (8) right cerebellar lobule Ⅶ b and right olfactory. Furthermore, total depressive symptom scores were negatively correlated with RS-FC between multiple brain regions, including the left superior frontal gyrus and right middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.72, p < 0.001), left superior frontal gyrus and left temporal pole middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.69, p < 0.001), left triangular inferior frontal gyrus and left temporal pole middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.65, p < 0.001), left medial superior frontal gyrus and right middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.65, p < 0.001), left insula and right cerebellar crus II (r = -0.6, p < 0.001), and right superior temporal gyrus and right cerebellar crus II (r = -0.67, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest preliminary associations between depressive symptoms and altered RS-FC in lung cancer patients, with connectivity changes correlating with symptom severity. However, because data on psychotropic medication use, cancer-related symptoms (e.g., pain, fatigue), and treatment details were not systematically collected, these findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive markers of comorbid depression. Future longitudinal studies with systematic assessment of medication, treatment, and multidimensional symptom burden are needed to determine whether these connectivity patterns specifically reflect depressive symptoms or broader cancer-related sequelae.

papers.title_zh: 表观遗传与活性氧交互网络驱动肿瘤放疗抵抗的机制综述及分型组合治疗策略框架
papers.title_en: Interplay Between Epigenetics and Reactive Oxygen Species in Tumor Radioresistance: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Strategies for Radiotherapy.
papers.authors: Yang Z, Wang J, Wang G, Zhu J, Zhang S, Guo W
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical and Radiation Oncology, The Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Wenzhou, Peo…
papers.authors_conclusion: Strategically targeting the epigenetics-ROS network offers a transformative paradigm for overcoming radioresistance and personalizing cancer radiotherapy.
papers.ai_note: 全文为叙述性综述，摘要未报告检索策略、文献筛选流程、纳入排除标准或任何定量合成，却自称“systematically synthesizes”，属方法学表述与设计不匹配；三大核心原则（stress adaptation / malignant reinforcement / contextual determinacy）与四层调控机制、四类分型组合策略均为作者提出的概念框架，摘要中无支持性数据或证据等级标注；结尾“transformative paradigm”为乐观表述，超出综述所能提供的证据强度。文中自列的五项转化障碍（含preclinical-clinical discordance）实际上也削弱了其临床转化主张。
papers.reason: 为放疗抵抗的机制研究提供“表观遗传-ROS”双向回路与分型匹配策略的概念地图，可用于设计放疗增敏联合方案的假设生成与分层思路，但无临床决策级证据，不宜直接改变胸外科/胸部肿瘤的临床判断。
papers.abstract_en: Radiotherapy efficacy is constrained by tumor radioresistance, which arises in part from the interplay between reactive oxygen species (ROS) and epigenetic regulation. This review systematically synthesizes the bidirectional "epigenetics-ROS interactive network" that governs tumor radiosensitivity. We propose that this network operates through three core principles: stress adaptation (acute ROS triggers transient epigenetic adjustments for redox recovery), malignant reinforcement (chronic ROS drives stable epigenetic reprogramming toward therapy resistance), and contextual determinacy (cellular outcomes depend on integrated ROS-epigenetic patterns rather than individual signals). Mechanistically, we delineate four regulatory layers including DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, and chromatin remodeling, through which the epigenetic machinery controls ROS homeostasis, and conversely, how radiation-induced ROS reshape the epigenetic landscape via oxidative modification of epigenetic enzymes and signaling pathways. These bidirectional interactions form feedback circuits that ultimately dictate whether cells undergo repair, senescence, apoptosis, or ferroptosis. Based on this mechanism, we propose a context-dependent decision framework that matches four distinct combination strategies (ROS amplification, epigenetic priming, hypoxia relief, and multi-pathway cell death induction) with four tumor subtypes defined by their oxidative and epigenetic profiles. We also identify five translational roadblocks including toxicity, delivery inefficiency, manufacturing scalability, regulatory uncertainty, and preclinical-clinical discordance. Resolving these barriers is essential for unlocking the therapeutic potential of this regulatory axis. Strategically targeting the epigenetics-ROS network offers a transformative paradigm for overcoming radioresistance and personalizing cancer radiotherapy.

papers.title_zh: 基于电子健康数据的胰腺癌风险预测模型早期检测的前瞻性试点可行性研究：入组率8.2%，18个月影像与CA19-9完成率79%
papers.title_en: Implementation of Risk Prediction Models Using Electronic Health Data for Early Detection of Pancreatic Cancer: A Prospective Pilot Feasibility Study.
papers.authors: Wu BU, Luong TQ, Lustigova E, Jeon C, Puttock EJ, Moon RH, Munis MA, Chen W et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Research and Evaluation, Southern California Permanente Medical Group, Pasadena, California, USA.
papers.results: 1251例符合条件者中102例入组（8.2%）；基线影像完成89/102（87%），基线CA19-9完成98/102（96%）；18个月时79%完成影像和CA19-9两者；10/102（10%）因影像发现接受额外临床评估；基线CA19-9升高者18%
papers.authors_conclusion: Real-time EHR-based ML algorithms can be combined with blood- and imaging-based surveillance for early detection of PC with acceptable burden of incidental findings. However, improved patient engagement is a key aspect that will need to be addressed in order to successfully scale an AI-guided strategy for early detection.
papers.ai_note: 研究仅报告可行性指标，未报告胰腺癌检出率、分期迁移或筛查相关临床结局；8.2%入组率很低，摘要仍以“可接受负担”和“可结合”作为主要口径，对规模化可行性的乐观表述需谨慎；10%额外评估未说明其中恶性/良性结果及伤害；无对照且样本量小，无法评估风险模型的实际早期检测效能。

pico.p: 50-84岁、基于4个既往验证模型估算18个月胰腺癌风险≥1%的成人，2021年1月至2023年3月识别；1251例符合条件，102例入组（中位年龄69岁[IQR 62-75]；58%女性；48% Hispanic、34% White、11% Black、7% Asian）
pico.ic: 干预：EHR-based机器学习/回归风险预测联合基线及18个月横断面影像和CA19-9检测；对照：无（单臂可行性研究）

papers.reason: 为EHR/机器学习驱动的胰腺癌早期检测提供前瞻性实施与入组可行性基线，但疾病领域非胸部肿瘤，对胸外科临床判断直接影响有限；可作为数字筛查研究中入组率、随访完成度和偶发发现负担的方法学参照。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We previously developed multiple machine-learning and regression-based risk prediction models using retrospective electronic health records (EHR) to estimate near-term risk of pancreatic cancer (PC). This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of an early detection strategy combining initial EHR-based risk prediction with downstream imaging and blood-based testing. METHODS: This prospective study included adults aged 50-84 years with an estimated ≥ 1% 18-month risk of PC, identified between January 2021 and March 2023 using four previously validated models. Patients with a history or active suspicion of PC were excluded. Participants completed cross-sectional imaging and CA19-9 Labs at baseline and again at 18 months. Outcomes included enrollment rates, test completion rate, and burden of incidental findings. RESULTS: Of 1251 eligible patients, 102 (8.2%) enrolled (median age 69 years [IQR 62-75]; 58% women; 48% Hispanic, 34% White, 11% Black, and 7% Asian). At baseline, 89 (87%) completed imaging and 98 (96%) completed CA19-9. At 18 months, 79% completed both imaging and CA19-9. Ten (10%) participants underwent additional clinical evaluations triggered by imaging findings. Evaluations included an endoscopic ultrasound, renal imaging, and FibroScan. CA19-9 results were normal in most participants, though 18% had elevated levels at baseline. CONCLUSIONS: Real-time EHR-based ML algorithms can be combined with blood- and imaging-based surveillance for early detection of PC with acceptable burden of incidental findings. However, improved patient engagement is a key aspect that will need to be addressed in order to successfully scale an AI-guided strategy for early detection.

papers.authors: Szydlarska D, Lewtak K, Ciechomska MZ, Poznańska A, Śliwczyński A, Kanecki K
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Digital Medicine, Implementation and Innovation, National Medical Institute of the Ministry of the Interio…

papers.abstract_en: Background: Thyroid cancer (TC) is the most common endocrine malignancy, with a steadily increasing incidence observed worldwide. However, temporal trends and demographic patterns may vary across populations. Objectives: To assess hospital-based incidence rates, demographic characteristics, and selected epidemiological patterns of TC in Poland between January 2012 and December 2024. Material and Methods: This population-based, retrospective study utilized hospitalization records of TC patients in Poland obtained from the Nationwide General Hospital Morbidity Study. Only first-time hospitalizations in the study period with reported primary or secondary diagnoses of TC were included in the study. Results: The study cohort included 60,604 patients, and the mean annual hospital-based incidence rate was 12.2 per 100,000 inhabitants (95% CI: 11.0-13.4). The hospital-based incidence rate decreased from 15.2 in 2012 to 9.8 per 100,000 in 2020, followed by a marked increase, peaking to 16.6 per 100,000 in 2024. Women constituted 82.2% of cases, indicating a strong sex-related disparity. The mean age at diagnosis was 51.1 years (SD: 15.9). The mean age at diagnosis was 51.1 years (SD: 15.9), and a greater proportion of hospitalized thyroid cancer patients were urban than rural residents (67.4% vs. 32.6%). Marked regional variation was observed, with the highest rates recorded in selected northern and central voivodeships. Conclusions: TC hospitalization hospital-based incidence rates in Poland showed significant temporal variability, with the lowest rate in 2020, which may reflect disruptions in healthcare access during the COVID-19 pandemic and a possible diagnostic catch-up effect in subsequent years. Regional disparities may suggest the potential influence of environmental, socioeconomic, or healthcare-related factors.

papers.abstract_en: Large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) encompasses a biologically and clinically heterogeneous group of aggressive B-cell lymphomas, and outcomes remain poor in high-risk and relapsed/refractory settings. Beyond conventional anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies, the Fc-modified anti-CD19 antibody tafasitamab, the CD79b-directed antibody-drug conjugate polatuzumab vedotin, and CD20×CD3 bispecific antibodies are expanding treatment options across disease stages and patient populations. At the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, the phase 3 frontMIND trial provided randomized evidence for tafasitamab plus lenalidomide and R-CHOP in newly diagnosed high-risk disease, while OLYMPIA-3 further explored CD20×CD3 bispecific antibody intensification in the same setting. In older or treatment-unfit patients, early-phase nonrandomized studies of epcoritamab plus R-mini-CVP and mosunetuzumab monotherapy suggested the feasibility of chemotherapy-attenuated and chemotherapy-free approaches. In relapsed/refractory LBCL, SUNMO established a progression-free survival advantage for mosunetuzumab plus polatuzumab vedotin in autologous stem-cell transplantation (ASCT)-ineligible disease, whereas EPCORE NHL-2 supported epcoritamab-based salvage therapy in transplant-eligible patients. Collectively, these findings broaden the role of antibody-based regimens from frontline intensification and reduced-intensity treatment to nontransplant and transplant-directed salvage. Longer follow-up and randomized comparisons are needed to establish response durability, refine patient selection, and define optimal treatment sequencing.

papers.abstract_en: The immune system integrates signals to regulate immune responses, forming complex context-dependent networks where identical cues produce distinct outcomes. Signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) transcription factors convert cytokine receptor engagement into transcriptional responses, serving as central regulatory hubs. How concurrent STAT activation across different environments shapes immune cell function remains unclear. Here, we show that STAT3 plays a context-dependent role in antiviral natural killer (NK) cells, either promoting or impairing adaptive responses depending on the inflammatory milieu during mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) infection. STAT3 is recruited to distinct genomic loci depending on IL-15 or type I interferon availability, thus driving alternative transcriptional programs. Mechanistically, STAT3 differentially regulates downstream transcription factors MYB and B lymphocyte-induced maturation protein-1 (BLIMP-1) to shape NK cell differentiation during homeostasis and infection. STAT3 relocation is governed by epigenetic mechanisms and preferred relocation toward distinct STAT motifs. Thus, STAT3 functions as a cytokine-sensing transcriptional switch integrating IL-15 and type I interferon signals to control lymphocyte adaptation during viral infection.

papers.abstract_en: CTLA-4 is an inhibitory receptor on T cells that limits immune activation by competing with the co-stimulatory receptor CD28 for binding to CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) employ CTLA-4-mediated transendocytosis as a key suppressive mechanism. Several CTLA4 polymorphisms are associated with autoimmune disease risk and may modulate CTLA-4 expression and function. Here, we analyzed samples from 155 genotyped subjects using flow cytometry and functional assays to determine how haplotypes formed by 3 CTLA4 single-nucleotide polymorphisms shape T-cell phenotype and function ex vivo. The autoimmune-protective CTLA4 rs5742909-rs231775-rs3087243 CAA haplotype was linked to increased intracellular CTLA-4 expression in both Tregs and conventional CD4+ T cells compared with CGG, CAG, and TAG haplotypes, implicating rs3087243 as the likely causal variant. The CAA haplotype was also associated with increased Treg frequencies. In Tregs from CAA/CAA subjects, elevated steady-state CTLA-4 expression promoted enhanced early CTLA-4 surface mobilization following anti-CD3/anti-CD28 stimulation. Moreover, naïve Tregs from CAA/CAA subjects more effectively suppressed naïve CD4+ T-cell proliferation in the presence of CD80/CD86-expressing dendritic cells. Collectively, these findings indicate that the rs3087243-A-linked CAA haplotype is associated with increased CTLA-4 expression and enhanced Treg function, providing a mechanistic explanation for its protective association with autoimmunity.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies. However, strategies that improve the modularity and controllability of CAR signaling could broaden its applicability and safety across additional clinical contexts. Here, we describe a regulable CAR T-cell platform based on split intein-mediated protein trans-splicing (PTS) to conditionally reconstitute functional receptors in primary T-cells. METHODS: As a proof of concept, we engineered a split CAR targeting CD1a (NCT05679895), a surface antigen expressed in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL). The system consists of a membrane-anchored C-terminal scaffold containing the IMPDH.1C split intein fused to 4-1BB and CD3ζ signaling domains, and a soluble N-terminal adaptor composed of an anti-CD1a single-chain variable fragment (scFv) fused to the complementary IMPDH.1N split intein. RESULTS: Upon delivery of the adaptor module, the intein fragments undergo PTS, generating a functional membrane-bound CD1a CAR with splicing efficiencies of 85%. Reconstituted CAR T-cells exhibited antigen-specific cytotoxicity against CD1a+ T-ALL cells coupled to high levels of interferon-γ secretion. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that split intein-mediated CAR reconstitution enables a modular platform for conditional CAR reconstitution and transient control of receptor availability.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks among the leading global causes of death, with elderly patients facing heightened risks due to age-related declines in lung function. Breathlessness catastrophizing (BC), a negative cognitive response to dyspnea including rumination, magnification. Understanding the heterogeneity of BC in elderly COPD patients is essential for developing targeted interventions. AIMS: The objective of this study was to identify subgroups of elderly COPD patients with breathlessness catastrophizing through latent profile analysis (LPA) and to explore the related influencing factors. METHODS: The data of 225 elderly patients with COPD were collected and analyzed. The collected data included the demographic and clinical factors, and the patients were assessed with the Breathlessness Catastrophizing Scale(BCS), the COPD Self-Efficacy Scale(CSES) and the Ruminative Response Scale(RRS). RESULTS: The study identified three breathlessness catastrophizing subgroups: Low Breathlessness Catastrophizing Type(44.4%), Moderate Breathlessness Catastrophizing Type(25.8%), and High Breathlessness Catastrophizing Type(29.8%). Three factors were significantly associated with subgroups: number of COPD exacerbations in the past year, COPD self-efficacy, and rumination response (all p<0.05). Education level and daily steps significantly influenced the low breathlessness catastrophizing type (all p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Elderly COPD patients exhibit heterogeneity in breathlessness catastrophizing patterns. Factors including low education levels, frequent acute exacerbations, physical inactivity, diminished self-efficacy, and excessive rumination significantly increase the risk of severe breathlessness catastrophizing. Intervention strategies should prioritize enhancing self-efficacy, managing rumination, promoting physical activity, and implementing personalized approaches for different subgroups with breathlessness catastrophizing. Multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for reducing breathlessness catastrophizing and improving health outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Clinical trials are crucial for evidence generation on medicines. As of June, 2025, the European Union's (EU) clinical trial registries (Clinical Trial Information System and European Clinical Trial Register) housed data on nearly 55 000 clinical trials. The full potential of these data, especially when integrated with other sources such as real-world data, has remained mostly untapped for wider health-care innovation. In this Viewpoint, we report on the outcomes of an exploratory workshop with key stakeholders from across clinical research, held in Jan 25 and 26, 2024 under the Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) initiative. The workshop identified needs and potential use cases for the clinical trial registry data by gathering and analysing perspectives from diverse stakeholders. The analysis presented in this Viewpoint groups the use cases into three themes: optimising trial design and planning to leverage historical trial data for research optimisation; enhancing patient centricity to meet the diverse needs of patients; and strengthening the evaluation of evidence to maximise the collective effect of clinical trial data for regulatory, clinical, and policy decision making. Strong consensus emerged on key enablers for better use of data. These enablers were data standardisation to ensure consistent data representation among registries; data quality to enable reliable data analysis and decision making; interoperability to allow digital health systems to communicate seamlessly; and transparency to ensure data are made available to the public. As an initial step in addressing these needs, the European Medicines Agency developed the ACT EU trial map as a patient-oriented platform enabling easy trial discovery. The use cases identified at the workshop provide different starting points for supporting the setup of a clinical trial analytics ecosystem to enhance evidence-based decision making, foster innovation, guide funding, and ultimately benefit public health.

papers.abstract_en: Worldwide, liver cancer is the seventh most common cancer and the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality, reflecting its dismal prognosis, with only approximately 20% of patients alive 5 years after diagnosis. At least 50% of patients ultimately require systemic treatment. In 2020, the systemic treatment landscape changed dramatically with the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies, which have demonstrated improved overall survival and longer preservation of quality of life compared with tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)-based approaches. However, fewer than one third of patients achieve objective response, 10-25% experience severe immune-related adverse events, and ICI-based treatments represent a substantial economic burden for health systems. Importantly, robust and clinically validated predictive biomarkers of response to ICI remain an unmet need. This review summarizes current efforts to identify predictive biomarkers of ICI response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), integrating clinical, pathological, molecular, microbiome, and imaging approaches, and discusses how these developments may shape the future of treatment selection.

papers.abstract_en: Available evidence suggests that disruption of immune homeostasis may contribute to chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) beyond the effects of localized infection. This narrative review uses immune cells as its organizing axis and synthesizes recent evidence from single-cell sequencing, Mendelian randomization, and multi-omics. The available findings suggest that the M1/M2 dichotomy may not fully capture macrophage heterogeneity in prostatic tissues and that activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and IL-1β release may form a candidate link between innate immunity and the Th17 response. On this basis, the review discusses how glycolytic and oxidative-stress-related reprogramming may shape immune-cell states; considers chemokine networks such as CCL5/CCR5 and CXCL10/CXCR3 in the recruitment of macrophages, Th1 cells, and Th17 cells to prostatic tissue; and examines how mast cells and neurogenic inflammation may participate in the bidirectional neuro-immune dialogue associated with persistent pain. At the intervention level, we distinguish human clinical observations and interventions from findings in cell systems and animal models, and discuss candidate strategies involving the NLRP3 inflammasome, chemokine receptors, microbiota-derived metabolites, neuromodulation, and local or multi-component approaches. These concepts require prospective validation in clinically defined CP/CPPS subgroups before they can support mechanism-guided treatment.

papers.abstract_en: As the evening sets in and natural light fades to artificial light, it is remarkable how the colors around us still appear nearly the same. This phenomenon, known as color constancy, allows us to perceive relatively stable colors even as lighting conditions change. In the field of computer vision, replicating this human ability is the key to performing tasks such as recognizing objects and understanding scenes. This review examines two main approaches to tackle the challenge of computational color constancy: traditional static methods that rely on a set of assumptions about lighting and scene conditions, and newer learning-based methods that use models trained to estimate lighting directly from images. We look at how these techniques have evolved, from foundational methods like the gray-world assumption, which work within certain limitations, to modern deep learning techniques that can interpret lighting in more dynamic ways. The datasets, metrics, and reported results of the surveyed studies are consolidated into two comparative tables, providing a structured overview of the methods discussed. Together, these comparisons offer a broad perspective on how computational color constancy has developed and where it is headed, with particular emphasis on its applications in medical imaging.

papers.abstract_en: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is integral to emergency department (ED) care, but traditional order-based imaging workflows (OBIWs) are poorly aligned with unscheduled encounters and dynamic bedside imaging needs. We describe an accountable encounter-based imaging workflow (EBIW) that integrates patient identification, clinician attribution, encounter-linked image routing, and documentation accountability into a unified imaging informatics architecture. We performed a retrospective observational analysis of aggregated ED POCUS charge data from January 2018 through December 2025 at a single urban academic ED. Three sequential workflows were evaluated: a legacy electronic health record (EHR)-based OBIW, a POCUS Manager-based OBIW, and an accountable EBIW. The accountable EBIW links ultrasound images directly to the ED encounter using barcode-based patient and clinician identification and a centralized Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) router that generates an image availability message. This enables immediate image access in the picture archiving and communication system, EHR, and POCUS management platform before report completion. Charges were not used as a measure of reimbursement or financial return. Because a charge could only be generated after image archival, encounter linkage, documentation, and clinician attestation, charge capture served as a longitudinal system-level marker of completed workflow execution. Charges were normalized by ED visit volume and analyzed using interrupted time series analysis. Transition from the EHR-based OBIW to the POCUS Manager-based OBIW was not associated with an immediate increase in charges. Implementation of the accountable EBIW was associated with an immediate level increase of $11,746 per 1000 visits and a sustained positive quarterly slope thereafter. An accountable EBIW integrating encounter-level acquisition, DICOM routing, immediate image availability, clinician attribution, and documentation accountability was associated with improved capture of ED POCUS utilization.

papers.abstract_en: Over the past three decades, the biology of EIF3E (int6) has emerged as far more complex than originally anticipated. Initially identified as a common integration site of Mouse Mammary Tumor Virus (MMTV) and subsequently recognized as a component of the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 (eIF3) complex, EIF3E is now understood as a multifunctional regulator involved in selective mRNA translation, proteostasis, genome stability, cellular stress responses, and tissue homeostasis. Recent studies have further extended this framework by demonstrating that conditional Eif3e deficiency promotes lymphoma susceptibility in mice, providing in vivo evidence linking EIF3E-dependent translational regulation to immune homeostasis and cancer development. This focused review retraces the scientific journey of EIF3E from its discovery as int6 to the progressive definition of its diverse biological functions and context-dependent roles in cancer. Particular attention is given to the historical relationship between int6 (EIF3E) and int7 (RSPO2), whose unexpected reunion in recurrent EIF3E::RSPO2 fusions in human solid tumors provides a unique bridge between classical retroviral insertional mutagenesis and contemporary cancer genomics. While transcriptional activation of RSPO2 through EIF3E regulatory elements represents the established oncogenic mechanism of the fusion, whether disruption of one EIF3E allele exerts additional biological effects remains unknown. Together, these observations highlight EIF3E as a nexus between selective translation, cellular homeostasis, and cancer, while emerging links between epigenomic, epitranscriptomic, and translational regulation open new perspectives for understanding its context-dependent functions in tumorigenesis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for prevention of Ebola virus (EBOV) infection and disease (EVD). However, breakthrough EBOV infections have been observed in vaccinees. Currently available diagnostic and research assays cannot reliably distinguish individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus from those previously infected with the virus. This limitation complicates interpretation of vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and estimates of infection or attack rates. The ability to differentiate vaccine-induced immune responses from those resulting from natural infection remains an important unmet public health and research need. METHODS: We developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay simultaneously detecting IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus nucleoprotein (VSV-N), a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. We evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals after vaccination and 30 placebo (saline) recipients, as well as 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study. FINDINGS: We detected increase in all antibodies against both protein antigens in vaccinated individuals. Critically, the assay reveals that anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerge earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses in vaccinees, establishing anti-N IgA as a definitive, early, and durable biomarker of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity. INTERPRETATION: The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. Furthermore, the assay's adaptability to the expanding pipeline of VSV-vectored vaccines positions it as a transformative diagnostic platform for accelerating preparedness for future infectious disease threats and outbreak response strategies. FUNDING: Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the Divisions of Intramural Research (DIR) and Clinical Research (DCR) of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) at the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH).

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic lung disease (PH_lung) is a frequent complication of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung disease, and other parenchymal lung disorders, and is associated with impaired exercise capacity, reduced quality of life and poor survival. Despite increasing recognition of its clinical importance, major challenges remain regarding early diagnosis, hemodynamic classification, and optimal treatment. Following the 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension, a panel of experts reviewed from Germany and International collaborators summarized recent evidence and discussed unresolved issues relevant to everyday clinical practice. This review summarizes current concepts of the diagnosis and management of PH_lung, with particular emphasis on multimodal screening strategies integrating pulmonary function testing, biomarkers, echocardiography, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and thoracic imaging to improve patient selection for right heart catheterization. We discuss practical aspects of hemodynamic assessment, overlapping phenotypes, including connective tissue disease, sarcoidosis, and the emerging pulmonary vascular "lung phenotype", and current evidence supporting targeted therapies with emphasis on patients' pathways in real-world settings. While inhaled treprostinil has become the first approved treatment for pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease in several countries, no pulmonary hypertension-specific therapy is currently recommended routinely for COPD-associated PH, highlighting the need for careful patient phenotyping and individualized management in expert centres. The review further addresses indications for lung transplantation and outlines future research priorities. Earlier recognition, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continued translational and clinical research are essential to improve outcomes in this highly vulnerable patient population.

papers.abstract_en: Digital three-dimensional (3D) visualization is an evolving field that is being introduced into pediatric surgical oncology, where it addresses challenges related to complex anatomy and difficulties accurately defining surgical margins. This paper provides an overview of digital 3D modeling in pediatric surgical oncology and explores ways to further advance this field. Digital 3D models may improve various aspects of surgery, such as preoperative planning, intraoperative guidance, patient education, and surgical training. Traditionally, 3D models are manually or semi-automatically segmented. More recently, artificial intelligence (AI) can automatically segment pediatric solid tumors. For preoperative planning, 3D models improve anatomic understanding and help multidisciplinary communication. During surgery, these models can assist the surgeon in accurately localizing tumors and determining resection margins in preclinical research settings. In patient education, 3D models present an opportunity to improve patient understanding of disease, therapy, and surgical risks. Lastly, digital 3D models are used in surgical training, particularly for challenging cases. Although digital 3D technologies are evaluated using technical performance metrics, these measures do not necessarily result in improved clinical outcomes. Consequently, evidence demonstrating improved surgical outcomes remains limited, also due to the small patient cohorts. Several challenges continue to hinder clinical translation, including image quality and standardization, segmentation complexity, organ deformability during surgery, and insufficient clinical validation. Addressing these limitations will require progress in four key areas: AI integration, multicenter validation, the development of centralized infrastructures including digital twins, and scalable implementation strategies that support widespread clinical adoption.

papers.abstract_en: Hedysarum polysaccharide (HPS), the major bioactive constituent of Radix Hedysari, possesses anti-inflammatory activity; however, few studies have explored its application for ulcerative colitis (UC). In this study, HPS-80 was extracted using combined complex-enzyme hydrolysis and ultrasonication. We further evaluated its preventive effects and underlying mechanisms in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC model in C57BL/6 mice. Results showed HPS-80 significantly improved DSS-induced UC symptoms (weight loss, hematochezia, colon shortening) and reduced Disease Activity Index (DAI). Mechanistically, it inhibited pro-inflammatory factors Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha(TNF-α),Interleukin-6, (IL-6), alleviated oxidative stress, upregulated tight junction proteins occludin, claudin-1(ZO-1), and modulated intestinal microbiota (suppressed harmful bacteria like Bacteroidota, enriched beneficial ones like Firmicutes and Akkermansia). Conclusion: HPS-80 exerts protective effects against UC via anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and gut-microbiota-regulating capacities. It is a promising candidate agent for UC prevention.

papers.abstract_en: Traumatic abdominal wall hernia (TAWH) is an uncommon but clinically important consequence of both blunt and penetrating abdominal trauma. It is defined by disruption of the abdominal wall musculature and fascia with herniation of intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal contents through the defect. Although penetrating abdominal wall defects are usually apparent and can often be primarily closed during operative exploration, blunt TAWH is significantly more heterogeneous and challenging. The skin may remain intact while the muscle, fascia, neurovascular supply, and bony attachments are disrupted. The reported incidence of TAWH varies according to imaging strategy and trauma population, but frank herniation remains rare, occurring in <1% of blunt trauma patients in most contemporary series. The major management challenge is deciding whether the patient requires immediate trauma laparotomy or laparoscopy, acute abdominal wall repair, staged management with same-admission repair, or delayed hernia repair/abdominal wall reconstruction. Evidence remains primarily dominated by retrospective single-center series, multicenter registry studies, and systematic reviews with heterogeneous definitions and follow-up. Although traditional dogma had taught that these repairs should always be performed in a delayed fashion, recent multicenter data, systematic reviews, and surgeon experience suggest that timing of repair, type of repair, and mesh use must be individualized; bowel injury, contamination, defect location, and patient physiology are more important than a universal early-versus-delayed algorithm. This article summarizes the practical issues the trauma and acute care surgeon needs to know: diagnosis, classification, associated injuries, indications for exploration, repair timing, operative strategy, management of lateral and posterior defects, mesh use in contaminated fields, and associated outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: The management of advanced, recurrent extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma has shifted toward prolonged systemic therapy including immune checkpoint inhibition. Incorporating local treatment for oligometastatic or oligoprogressive disease without interrupting systemic therapy remains challenging. Conventional liver-directed therapies frequently require a chemotherapy break. Histotripsy is a noninvasive, non-thermal, non-ionizing modality that permits continuation of systemic therapy. This case presents a 71-year-old woman with recurrent extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who developed multifocal hepatic metastases while receiving gemcitabine and durvalumab. She was deemed not a candidate for further radiation therapy or other locoregional therapies; thus, nine of ten hepatic lesions were treated with histotripsy in a single session. This case highlights the possibility of integrating histotripsy with chemoimmunotherapy by providing short-term local control of oligometastatic progression without the need to interrupt systemic treatment.Level of Evidence: Level 4, Case Report.
